Market context
South African operating context
South Africa offers substantial mineral resources, mining and engineering expertise, established 
contractors and supporting infrastructure. Government is also seeking to stimulate exploration and 
critical-mineral development, with copper included in its Critical Minerals and Metals Strategy.
The South African mining environment continues to evolve. Mining projects have to navigate 
regulatory requirements, infrastructure constraints and security considerations, alongside important 
commitments to transformation, employment, procurement, skills development and communities. 
Improvements in electricity reliability and reforms to freight infrastructure and mineral-rights 
administration are encouraging, with effective implementation expected to support further progress.
Northern Cape context
Our projects are located in established Northern Cape mining districts with existing mining knowledge 
and infrastructure. The region’s strong solar and wind resources also provide opportunities to reduce 
future energy costs and carbon intensity.
Water availability remains an important consideration. Currency movements also affect project 
economics, with revenues largely linked to US-dollar commodity prices and a significant proportion of 
costs expected to be South African Rand-denominated.
Global copper: Structural demand meets constrained supply
Copper demand is being supported by investment in electricity networks, renewable energy, electric 
vehicles, digital infrastructure and traditional industrial uses. The International Energy Agency expects 
copper to record the largest growth in volume among critical minerals to 2040, while warning that mine 
supply could be around 25% short of primary copper requirements by 2035.
Supply growth is constrained by declining ore grades, higher project costs, fewer major discoveries 
and long development lead times. This is increasing the value of advanced projects with credible 
pathways to production.
Copper prices remain cyclical and are influenced by Chinese economic activity, global manufacturing 
and construction, inventories, exchange rates and investor sentiment. Zinc provides us with additional 
exposure to infrastructure and industrial demand.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive
No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`, note references) or small-print footnote definitions appear in the supplied D002 evidence `[D002, physical PDF p. 9]`. The qualifications present are embedded in body text rather than footnotes, and each carries forecast-relevant caveats:

- **"revenues largely linked to US-dollar commodity prices and a significant proportion of costs expected to be South African Rand-denominated"** `[D002, physical PDF p. 9]`. This is a directional FX exposure statement, not a quantified hedge or sensitivity. It implies a ZAR-cost / USD-revenue margin structure, so a weaker ZAR is margin-accretive and a stronger ZAR is margin-dilutive. It does **not** state the split of USD vs ZAR costs, nor whether any hedging or price-contingent contracts exist. Must be verified against the CFO review and financial notes (FX rates used, hedging disclosures, cost currency split).
- **"Water availability remains an important consideration"** `[D002, physical PDF p. 9]`. Unquantified operational risk flag. No volume, licence, or mitigation detail is given here; needs verification against the business reviews (D008) for water rights/secured supply and any production constraint.
- **"Improvements in electricity reliability and reforms to freight infrastructure and mineral-rights administration are encouraging, with effective implementation expected to support further progress"** `[D002, physical PDF p. 9]`. Forward-looking and conditional ("expected to"), not a committed input. Should not be modelled as a cost or volume benefit without corroboration in D007/D008.
- **"mine supply could be around 25% short of primary copper requirements by 2035"** and **"largest growth in volume among critical minerals to 2040"** `[D002, physical PDF p. 9]`. Third-party (IEA-attributed) long-run market framing, not company guidance. No price deck, discount rate, or forecast horizon is attached here — so it cannot be used as a forecast input without the study assumptions in later sections.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **`* All-in sustaining costs` — attached to "US$0.94/lb AISC*"** `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]`. The footnote only expands the acronym; it does **not** state the AISC methodology, what is included/excluded (by-product credits, sustaining capex, G&A, royalties), the period, or the copper/zinc price and FX deck underpinning it. This is a headline valuation-grade number presented without definition — it must be reconciled to the APM section and the study/technical report before use in the model.
- **`* Pre optimisation net present value (post-tax)` — attached to "A$75m NPV*" for Okiep Flat Mines** `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]`. Critical qualification: the NPV is **pre-optimisation** and therefore not a current base case; no discount rate, price deck, capex, mine life, or production profile is given. The "Production targeted from 2028" claim sits alongside an NPV that management itself flags as superseded by pending optimisation — treat the A$75m as a floor/indicative figure only.
- **"subject to the satisfaction of applicable conditions precedent" — Glencore prepayment** `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]`. The US$250m facility is described as **binding but conditional**; no conditions precedent, drawdown schedule, repayment mechanics (of-take/off-take offset), security, or interest terms are disclosed here. This is the single largest funding item on the page and its conditionality is the key caveat.
- **"First production is targeted for Q3 2027"** `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]` — stated as a target with no contingency, ramp-up curve, or Uppers-vs-Deeps phasing detail. The "moving towards development" wording for Uppers and Deeps implies **not yet at FID/construction**, which sits in tension with a Q3 2027 first-production target and must be tested against the business review.
- **"31Mt resource"** `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]` — resource tonnage only; no grade, contained metal, reserve status, or classification is given. Cannot be used for production forecasting without the D009 statement.
- **"10Mt resource | 132kt contained copper"** (Okiep) `[D003, physical PDF p. 15]` — implies ~1.32% Cu head grade if 10Mt is the full resource base; no classification, recovery, or reserve conversion stated.
- **Enablers block capture warning**: the boundary crosses text and the layout is garbled; the "US$500k BHP Xplor equity-free funding" and IDC/Triple Flag references are legible but their exact attribution is uncertain due to the capture warning — treat as indicative pending re-read.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **`*` — "Volcanogenic massive sulphide"** `[D004, physical PDF p. 16]`: Pure acronym definition attached to "Top 30 Global VMS* ranking." It defines the deposit type only — it does **not** disclose the ranking source, methodology, dataset date, or whether the ranking is by contained metal, grade, or tonnage. The headline "Top 30 Global VMS" is therefore an unsupported comparative claim as captured. Verification required in D009 (resource statement) and/or D008 (business review) for the underlying resource tonnes/grade that would substantiate any ranking.

- **`**` — "Pre-optimisation post-tax net present value"** `[D004, physical PDF p. 16]`: This is the most consequential qualification on the page. It confirms the **A$75m Okiep value is explicitly pre-optimisation** — i.e., a superseded/placeholder number pending the optimisation study referenced in the same bullet ("With optimisation advancing"). Implications: (i) the A$75m should **not** be used as the forecast Okiep valuation without checking whether an optimised NPV has since been published; (ii) no discount rate, price deck, capex, mine life, or production profile is disclosed here, so the figure is not model-ready; (iii) direction of revision is unknown (optimisation could raise or lower NPV). Must be reconciled against D008 (Okiep business review) and any later study release.

- **"Refer ASX/JSE releases 28 March 2025 and 2 February 2026; and Investor Presentation 2 September 2026"** `[D004, physical PDF p. 16]`: The page's substantive claims (A$568m Prieska value, US$0.94/lb AISC, 4.8-yr payback, 213kt Cu/611kt Zn LOM, A$75m Okiep NPV, cost-quartile and VMS rankings) are **sourced externally to this annual report** — to prior ASX/JSE releases and an investor presentation not included in this capture. This means the annual report itself provides no in-document basis (price deck, discount rate, FX, recovery, capex) for these figures. Every headline number on D004 must be traced to its underlying study/release before use in the model. This is a critical forecast-integrity flag.

- **"Historic production" sourcing** `[D004, physical PDF p. 16]`: "Prieska historically delivered 430kt Cu and 1Mt Zn, while Okiep district produced in excess of 2Mt Cu" is sourced to Cairncross (2004) and "Company and Mine Records." These are **historic, not forecast**, figures and should not be conflated with the LOM contained-metal figures (213kt Cu / 611kt Zn) — note the historic Prieska 430kt Cu is roughly double the stated LOM 213kt Cu, a scale tension worth flagging (historic cumulative vs. current reserve-based LOM are different bases; confirm in D009).

- **No footnote text missing**: Both footnote markers (`*`, `**`) have their definitions present in this capture. No orphaned markers.

Having been involved with Orion since its early years, 
I have seen the Company evolve in scale, capability 
and ambition. This long-term perspective gives the 
Board a clear view of both how far the Company has 
come and the responsibilities that accompany its 
next stage of development.
For the Board, the focus is increasingly on ensuring 
that Orion has the governance, capability and 
discipline required to support delivery, manage risk 
and create long-term value for shareholders and 
other stakeholders.
Governance and accountability
During the year, the Board developed a detailed capability 
matrix to identify existing strengths and areas where 
additional expertise may be required. The Board and 
Committee Charters are also being updated, with greater 
emphasis on accountability, more formal reporting and 
effective oversight as the business grows.
The objective is to ensure that the Board has the right 
mix of skills and experience, receives the information 
it needs to assess performance effectively and can 
hold management accountable for delivery. Regular 
performance assessments of the Board and its 
committees will continue as part of this process.
As Orion continues to grow and transition towards 
development, we are reviewing our governance arrangements against the ASX Corporate Governance 
Council’s recommendations, including Board independence and committee structure, as part of the ongoing 
evolution of our governance framework.

--- Section D005 | original physical page 19 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified ---

From the Board’s perspective, one of the most 
significant developments during the year has 
been the continued progress with the Company’s

Shareholder support

Orion’s risk profile is evolving as the Company

The Board considers this important both from 
an operational perspective and in supporting the 
Company’s long-term licence to operate.

Q: Looking back on the financial year, what stands out most for you?
Firstly, we had a safe year. Safety is fundamental to the wellbeing of our people and to how we operate. 
Secondly, we have built an experienced and committed team capable of taking Orion into production.

target to first concentrate

During the year, we continued to address our funding base.

with the project plan.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`) or formal table notes appear in the supplied D007 evidence. However, several **embedded qualifications in body text** carry forecast-relevant caveats:

- **"including the potential for an early drawdown of up to US$50 million for early works, subject to the relevant conditions"** `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. This is a conditional, not committed, source of liquidity. It changes the interpretation of the US$250m headline: the immediately accessible amount is US$40m (Uppers) plus a *possible* US$50m early-works tranche, with US$210m (Deeps) gated behind later conditions. Forecast implication: near-term liquidity must not assume the US$50m until CPs confirmed. Verify in D008/D012 whether the early-works tranche is drawn or available.

- **"Substantial progress was made in satisfying the conditions required for Tranche A, including receipt of South African Reserve Bank approval and progress on the intercreditor and offtake arrangements"** `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. "Substantial progress" and "progress" are non-completion language. Tranche A is **not confirmed satisfied** as at 30 June 2026. This directly bears on Q29/Q32: funding close (and the 13-month construction clock) cannot be assumed to have started. Verify CP completion status and any long-stop date in D008/D012.

- **"The partial conversion of the IDC's ZAR344.5 million convertible loan facility into equity"** and **"The conversion also resulted in the release of the security previously granted to the IDC"** `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. Two implications: (i) the residual ZAR272.4m is now an **unsecured shareholder loan claim**, changing the debt/security stack and potentially the cost/priority of that funding; (ii) IDC is now an equity partner (23.8% PCZM HoldCo / ~16.7% effective Prieska), so future Prieska equity raises dilute IDC alongside Orion — relevant to dilution modelling. Verify loan terms (coupon, repayment, subordination) in D012.

- **"A further exploration expenditure commitment of approximately ZAR6.35 million remains for the acquired mineral projects"** `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. A hard, quantified near-term cash commitment at Okiep that must be added to the funding requirement and opex/exploration budget. Verify timing/period in D008/D012.

- **"This investment requirement is being considered together with our primary funding requirements at Prieska"** `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. Signals potential **competition for capital** between Okiep commitment and Prieska — a sequencing risk for the Okiep 2028 target. Verify in D008.

- **"Our financial risk profile will evolve as construction activity increases"** and FX paragraph `[D007, physical PDF p. 21]`. Confirms unhedged directional USD-funding / ZAR-spend mismatch is a live risk but gives no quantification. Verify hedge/sensitivity in D012.

Preparing for execution
Following completion of the Definitive Feasibility Study in March 
2025, the focus moved from defining the development concept to 
preparing the project for execution. 
The Prieska Mine Project Execution Plan was completed, supported 
by a Project Execution System designed to provide a standardised 
framework across scope, cost, schedule, quality, safety and 
sustainability. The Master Project Budget, Master Project 
Schedule and performance measures were also developed for 
implementation once funding is available.
The importance of this work extends beyond project administration. 
Prieska is preparing to move from a development project into 
a significantly larger construction and operating environment. 
Establishing clear responsibilities, controls and decision-making 
processes before activity accelerates is central to managing 
execution risk.
Refining the development sequence
Further value engineering during the year improved the sequencing of the Uppers development.
The final Upper-level mining schedule brings forward stoping tonnes from development completed 
during trial mining and allows Uppers mining to commence later than envisaged in the original schedule 
without affecting the planned processing timetable. This provides additional time for contractor 
mobilisation and equipment delivery while maintaining the overall development program.
The Uppers remain the first phase of production, with development of the Deeps planned to proceed 
in parallel. 

--- Section D008.1 | original physical page 23 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | Prieska Copper Zinc Mine ---
The two integrated phases 
Phase 1: Early production from the shallower, higher-grade Uppers while dewatering of the historic 
underground workings progresses in parallel. First concentrate is targeted approximately 
13 months after project funding becomes available.
Phase 2: Unlock the more extensive Deeps resource as dewatering, shaft rehabilitation and major 
infrastructure are completed. 
The Uppers are planned to provide the initial years of production, while development of the Deeps 
begins in parallel, extending Prieska into a full-scale operation with a 13.2-year Life of Mine.
Exploration will continue alongside development. Five extension targets have been identified at depth 
and are planned to be evaluated through underground drilling as access improves, providing further 
potential to expand the resource base and extend mine life.
This staged approach is designed to take Prieska from first production into a longer-life operation.

Preparing the existing infrastructure
Prieska benefits from its brownfields setting and established mining infrastructure, but bringing 
a mine that has been inactive for more than three decades back into operation requires detailed 
preparation.
Work during the year included commissioning dewatering infrastructure, clearing redundant 
equipment and services from the Hutchings Shaft and inspecting shaft infrastructure above the water 
level in preparation for future refurbishment.
Power and water requirements were also aligned with the staged development plan. Engagement 
with Eskom continued on the phased provision of Prieska’s future electricity requirements, while 
Orion, the Central Energy Corporation and the Siyathemba Local Municipality agreed on a framework 
for collaboration on the proposed expansion of the Orange River water extraction and treatment 
infrastructure.
The objective is to ensure that mine development, processing capacity and supporting infrastructure 
progress in a coordinated sequence as the project scales.
People and host community readiness
Operational readiness also extends to the workforce and host communities that will support the mine. 
Earlier training and trial mining activities established an important foundation for local participation. 
Around 405 local people completed an introduction to mining program, with 43 progressing to further 
competency training. During trial mining in 2023 and 2024, contractors also gave preference to 
suitable local candidates, helping the project achieve its aspirational target of 50% host-community 
employment. This experience provides a base for further training and workforce development as the 
project moves towards operations.

with local businesses to provide earlier visibility of potential opportunities, while support for a Mining 
Qualifications Authority-accredited training centre in Prieska is intended to strengthen the longer￾term local skills pipeline.

- **Status**: `Partially resolved (arithmetic tension flagged; D009 reconciliation still required)`
- **Answer & evidence**: The DFS box states Total Probable Ore Reserves 15.6Mt @ 1.1% Cu and 3.1% Zn → contained Cu 164kt and contained Zn 458kt [D008.1, p. 23]. Arithmetic check: 15.6Mt × 1.1% = 171.6kt Cu (stated 164kt, ~4.4% lower — consistent with rounding of tonnes/grade); 15.6Mt × 3.1% = 483.6kt Zn (stated 458kt, ~5.3% lower — same rounding direction). **However**, LOM contained metal is stated as Cu 213,055t and Zn 610,630t [p. 23] — i.e. LOM recovered metal *exceeds* reserve-contained metal by ~49kt Cu (+30%) and ~153kt Zn (+33%). This is only reconcilable if the LOM production schedule draws on material beyond the stated 15.6Mt probable reserve (e.g. Inferred/measured resource conversion, stockpiles, or the 31Mt total resource). This is a material inconsistency for forecasting — flag for D009.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote `*` — DFS source citation** [D008.1, p. 23]
- Text: "* Refer ASX/JSE release 28 March 2025"
- Effect: The entire DFS metric block (NPV A$568m, IRR 26%, payback 4.8 yrs, peak capital A$578m, AISC US$0.94/lb, capital intensity USD9,174/t Cu Eq pa) is **not independently supported within this annual report** — it is a cross-reference to an external release. Every assumption behind these numbers (price deck, discount rate, FX, recovery, sustaining capex) is outside this document. For forecasting, the A$568m NPV and 26% IRR must be treated as *unverified secondary figures* until D009 or D012 supplies the underlying assumptions. Critically, the NPV is dated to a March 2025 study — the annual report gives no indication of whether the NPV has been re-based to 30 June 2026 prices, costs or FX.

**Footnote `**` — AISC by-product basis** [D008.1, p. 23]
- Text: "** Assumes Zn revenue is a by-product credit"
- Effect: This is the single most consequential qualification in the section. It converts the headline "AISC US$0.94/lb Cu" from a co-product cost into a **zinc-credit-netted copper cost**. Implications:
  1. The metric is levered to the zinc price and to the Zn:Cu price ratio — a fall in zinc price raises the copper AISC even with flat copper.
  2. It is **not** comparable to peer AISC figures reported on a co-product basis, which undermines any "lowest cost quartile" framing (Q16).
  3. It says nothing about sustaining capex treatment, royalties, or FX — all of which must be checked in the APM reconciliation (Q11 → D012).
  4. The LOM zinc output (610,630t contained Zn vs 213,055t Cu [p. 23]) is large relative to copper, so the by-product credit is a *material* share of the cost offset, not a marginal one.

**Qualification — "13 months after project funding becomes available"** [D008.1, p. 23]
- This is a **conditional, relative** schedule, not a calendar commitment. It embeds an unstated funding-close date. Any forecast of first concentrate must therefore be built as: (assumed funding close) + 13 months. The section explicitly confirms funding was *not* available at 30 June 2026 [p. 24], so the 13-month clock had not started at balance date. This is a hard constraint on FY27–FY28 production modelling.

**Qualification — revised Uppers schedule** [D008.1, p. 22]
- "The final Upper-level mining schedule brings forward stoping tonnes from development completed during trial mining and allows Uppers mining to commence later than envisaged in the original schedule without affecting the planned processing timetable."
- Effect: This is a **de-risking of the front-end schedule** (later Uppers mining start, offset by pre-developed stoping tonnes) but it also implies the original schedule had Uppers mining starting earlier than now planned. It does **not** change the 13-month-to-first-concentrate target, and it does not change peak capital. It does, however, mean the *ramp-up profile* differs from the March 2025 DFS — a forecast built on the DFS ramp-up curve would be wrong. The revised curve is not disclosed here.

**Qualification — B-O-O-T concentrator "subject to funding, final approvals and execution"** [D008.1, p. 23]
- The ENPROTEC contract is **not executed**. "Substantially progressed" [p. 24] is not "signed". This is a live execution risk: the 20,000tpm Uppers concentrator is on the critical path to first concentrate, and its commercial terms (lease/operating payments vs capex, term, termination) are undisclosed. If B-O-O-T payments are opex, peak capital of A$578m may understate total cash commitment; if capex, the A$578m may already include it. Unresolved.

**Qualification — "pre-execution phase" at 30 June 2026** [D008.1, p. 24]
- This is a direct contradiction of any reading that construction has begun. No FID, no construction declaration, no mobilisation. For forecasting, FY26 Prieska spend is development/readiness only; FY27 spend depends entirely on funding close.

**Qualification — water and power are "frameworks" and "engagement", not secured supply** [D008.1, p. 23]
- "agreed on a framework for collaboration on the proposed expansion of the Orange River water extraction and treatment infrastructure" and "Engagement with Eskom continued on the phased provision". Neither is a supply agreement, licence, or costed scope. Both are potential permitting/utilities bottlenecks to first concentrate and are unquantified in capex.

**Missing footnote check**: No footnote markers appear in this capture without a corresponding definition. The two markers present (`*`, `**`) are both defined on p. 23. No missing-footnote flag required for D008.1.

During the year, the project team completed an evaluation to

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **`*` on "Okiep Flat Mines Definitive Feasibility Study*" and the DFS metric block** [D008.2, p. 25]: The footnote reads "*Refer ASX/JSE release 28 March 2025." This is the single most consequential qualification in the section. It means **every DFS number on p. 25 (10Mt @ 1.3% Cu resource / 132kt Cu; 6.1Mt @ 1.2% Cu probable reserve / 71kt Cu; LOM concentrate 261,133 dmt / 78,340t contained Cu; NPV A$75m; IRR 19%; payback 5.3 yrs; peak capital A$103m; AISC US$2.39/lb; capital intensity US$10,383/t Cu pa) is sourced to an external March 2025 release and is NOT restated for the FY26 optimisation work described in the same section.** The section explicitly says the optimisation is intended to "lower upfront capital requirements" and improve economics, yet the headline DFS metrics are the old, pre-optimisation set. For forecasting, the A$103m peak capital and A$75m NPV must be treated as **stale pending an updated development case** — the company states the updated case "will determine the pathway... and, ultimately, construction" [p. 25]. Verification required: whether D009/D012 restate Okiep capex/NPV, and whether the March 2025 release assumptions (discount rate, Cu price deck, FX, recovery) are disclosed anywhere in the annual report.

- **`*` on drill holes OFMED157 and OFMED158** [D008.2, p. 26]: Footnote marker present but **the footnote definition is NOT present in this section capture** — the text shows "OFMED157* and OFMED158*" with no corresponding footnote text supplied. This is likely a cross-reference to a separate ASX/JSE drilling-results release (as with the DFS asterisk), but I will not guess. Verification question raised: locate the footnote definition / source release for OFMED157–158 in D009 or D012.

- **`**` on OFMED153** [D008.2, p. 26]: Same issue — double-asterisk marker on "OFMED153**" with **no footnote definition in the supplied evidence**. The 49.35m @ 5.05% Cu (incl. 21.66m @ 9.41% Cu) intercept is a prior-hole reference; its source/date is unverified. Verification question raised.

- **Embedded qualification — "potential" language on alternative shaft access** [p. 25]: "Initial work on alternative shaft access... **indicated the potential to** reduce waste-incline development, development duration, and initial capital requirements." This is aspirational, not a quantified saving. It changes interpretation of the A$103m peak capital: the company is signalling **downside** to capex is possible but has not booked it. Forecast treatment: keep A$103m as base case, flag potential reduction as an upside sensitivity pending the updated development case.

- **Embedded qualification — resource vs reserve gap** [p. 25]: Resource 10Mt @ 1.3% Cu = 132kt contained Cu; probable reserve 6.1Mt @ 1.2% Cu = 71kt contained Cu. LOM contained Cu production is **78,340t**, which **exceeds** probable reserve contained Cu (71kt) by ~7.3kt (~10%). This mirrors the Prieska pattern (Q18/Q47) — LOM production exceeds reserve contained metal, implying non-reserve feed or a recovery/contained-metal definition mismatch. Arithmetic check: 6.1Mt × 1.2% = 73.2kt in-situ; stated 71kt (rounding/grade precision); LOM 78.34kt recovered > 71kt reserve contained — **mathematically impossible if LOM feed is reserve-only at ≤100% recovery**. Must reconcile in D009.

- **Arithmetic check — capital intensity** [p. 25]: US$10,383/t Cu (pa). If peak capital A$103m and LOM contained Cu 78,340t over LOM years: US$10,383 × 78,340 ≈ US$813m — far above A$103m (~US$56m at ~0.55 USD/AUD). The "per annum" basis implies annual Cu output, not LOM. Implied annual Cu ≈ A$103m×FX / US$10,383. At ~0.55 USD/AUD: US$56.7m / 10,383 ≈ 5,460 t Cu/yr → LOM ≈ 78,340/5,460 ≈ 14.3 years. This is a **derived** mine life (~14 yrs) not stated in the section — flag as a verification question for D009 (actual LOM years and annual production profile).

--- Section D008.3 | original physical page 27 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | BHP Xplor: advancing district-scale understanding ---
A significant development during the year was Orion Minerals’ selection for the 2026 BHP Xplor 
program, from more than 600 applicants and as the only company working in Africa in the cohort.
The program combines funding, technical collaboration and access to specialist expertise to accelerate 
exploration thinking and improve target generation.
This is particularly relevant in the Northern Cape. Although much of the surface geology is well mapped, 
large prospective areas are obscured by Kalahari sands and Karoo sediments, while significant historic 
exploration predates many of the geophysical techniques now available.
Modern exploration provides an opportunity to investigate both known systems and concealed geology 
at a scale and depth not readily accessible to earlier explorers.
Work during the year included district-scale magnetotelluric surveys, geochemical and isotopic studies, 
development of regional spatial datasets and further processing and interpretation of geophysical 
information.

--- Section D008.3 | original physical page 27 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | BHP Xplor: advancing district-scale understanding ---
Building the longer-term pipeline
Exploration also continued across the wider Areachap portfolio.
Orion Minerals’ tenements cover more than 2,700 km² of the 
Areachap Belt and include multiple copper-zinc and nickel-copper￾cobalt-PGE-gold targets.
The portfolio includes:
• Kantienpan, where drill testing has identified substantial 
zinc-copper mineralisation.
• Witkop, where the copper-gold opportunity remains under 
assessment.
• Boksputs, where additional follow-up work is required.
• The Orange River pegmatite swarm, where lithium, beryllium 
and rare earth element potential is being investigated.
• Jacomynspan, which has an existing JORC Mineral 
Resource.

--- Section D008.3 | original physical page 27 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | BHP Xplor: advancing district-scale understanding ---
Year-end position and next steps
By year-end, our exploration program was more closely aligned 
with our development priorities, focusing on opportunities 
that can strengthen the projects closest to development while 
continuing to build the longer-term pipeline.
The next phase will focus on extending resources and mine-life 
potential at Prieska and Okiep, integrating the results of the BHP 
Xplor program into regional targeting, and continuing to assess 
the wider portfolio according to its potential contribution to 
future growth.

--- Section D008.3 | original physical page 27 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | BHP Xplor: advancing district-scale understanding ---
Australian projects
We have interests in two Australian projects, providing exposure to additional exploration upside while 
our primary focus remains on advancing our South African assets. The Australian assets provide 
longer-term optionality without requiring significant near-term investment from us.
At the Fraser Range Project in Western Australia, we have a 35% interest in a joint venture with IGO 
Limited and Geological Resources Pty Ltd. The project is located within a highly prospective nickel 
copper-cobalt sulphide belt that hosts IGO’s Nova-Bollinger operation. 
Under the joint venture arrangements, IGO is responsible for funding and carrying out exploration 
through to completion of the first Pre-Feasibility Study, allowing Orion to retain exposure to the project 
without ongoing funding commitment. 
In Victoria, we have full ownership of the Walhalla Gold and Polymetals Project. The Walhalla-Woods 
Point district is prospective for gold and high-grade copper, nickel and PGE mineralisation. No field or 
exploration activities were undertaken at Walhalla during the year, reflecting the prioritisation of our 
Northern Cape projects.

- **No footnote markers, table notes, or superscript references appear in the D008.3 capture** [D008.3, physical PDF p. 27]. - **Embedded qualification — "without requiring significant near-term investment from us" (Australian projects)** [D008.3, physical PDF p. 27]: This is a forward-looking, unquantified qualification. It implies near-zero Australian exploration capex in the forecast period, but "significant" is undefined and no dollar cap is given. It also implies Orion carries **no funding obligation** at Fraser Range until the first PFS is complete (IGO funds through PFS). Verification required: confirm in D012 that no Australian exploration expenditure or JV cash-call liability is recorded, and confirm the 35% interest is not subject to dilution/earn-in obligations that could trigger future cash outflow.

- **Embedded qualification — "No field or exploration activities were undertaken at Walhalla during the year"** [D008.3, physical PDF p. 27]: Confirms zero FY26 spend at Walhalla. Forecast implication: Walhalla carries holding costs only (tenement/administration), not exploration burn. Verify in D012 whether any impairment indicator or carrying value exists for Walhalla given nil activity.

- **Embedded qualification — "exploration program was more closely aligned with our development priorities"** [D008.3, physical PDF p. 27]: Signals a **reprioritisation of exploration spend toward Prieska/Okiep resource extension** and away from grass-roots/greenfield work. Forecast implication: exploration expenditure should be modelled as near-mine/resource-extension weighted, not district-greenfield weighted. No quantum given — verify total exploration spend and its split in D012/D011.

- **Embedded qualification — "Jacomynspan, which has an existing JORC Mineral Resource"** [D008.3, physical PDF p. 27]: A JORC resource is asserted but **no tonnage, grade, or contained-metal figure is given**, and it is not stated whether it is included in the D009 Ore Reserves and Mineral Resources Statement. Verification required in D009: confirm whether Jacomynspan is reported in the group Mineral Resources table and on what basis (attributable %, classification).

Orion reports Exploration Results, Mineral 
Resource and Ore Reserve Estimates in 
accordance with the ASX Listing Rules 
and the requirements and guidelines of the 
Australasian Code for Reporting Exploration 
Results, Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves, 
2012 (the JORC Code). 
The JSE requires reporting in terms of the South 
African Code for the Reporting of Exploration 
Results, Mineral Resources and Mineral 
Reserves, 2016 (SAMREC Code). However, the 
JORC Code requirements are considered similar 
enough to be accepted by the JSE. The Orion 
financial year end is 30 June and all subsidiaries 
have been aligned to this annual reporting date. 
The 2026 Annual Report covers Orion’s 
exploration projects in the Areachap and Okiep 
areas in the Northern Cape Province of South 
Africa, as well as its interest in a number of 
Australian projects. By the end of FY2018, 
Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources 
were classified and reported from both Orion’s 
flagship Prieska Copper Zinc Mine (refer ASX/
JSE releases 8 February 2018 and 9 April 2018), 
as well as the Jacomynspan Nickel-Copper

Mineral Resources had been upgraded to 
Probable Mineral Ore Reserves, Indicated 
Mineral Resources and Inferred Mineral 
Resources for both the near surface +105 Level 
Mineral Resource (refer ASX/JSE releases 
15 January 2019 and 26 June 2019) and the 
underground Deep Sulphide Mineral Resource 
(refer ASX/JSE releases 18 December 2018 and 
26 June 2019).
The Prieska Deep Sulphide and +105 Level Ore 
Reserve was updated in FY2020 (refer ASX/JSE 
release 26 May 2020) and again in 2025 (refer 
ASX/JSE release 28 March 2025).

Firstly, the Competent Persons’ responsibility for public reporting:
• must be current members of a professional organisation that is recognised in the JORC Code 
framework
• must have at least five years’ relevant experience in the style of mineralisation and reporting 
activity for which they are acting as a Competent Person
• must have given a written consent for inclusion of the results and estimates that are reported, 
stating that the report agrees with supporting documentation regarding the results or estimates 
prepared by each Competent Person 
• must have prepared supporting documentation for results and/or estimates to a level consistent 
with standard industry practices 
This includes JORC Table 1 checklists for any results and/or estimates reported. 
Orion also ensures that any publicly reported results and/or estimates are prepared using JORC 
and ASX guidelines, and accepted industry methods using specialised guidance for aspects where 
required, such as metal prices and foreign exchange rates. Estimates and results are also peer￾reviewed internally by Orion’s senior technical staff before being presented to Orion’s Board for 
approval and subsequent ASX reporting. 
Market-sensitive or production-critical estimates may also be audited by suitably qualified external 
consultants to ensure the precision and correctness of the reported information. Once operational, 
Orion plans to ensure that the estimation precision of actual mine and process production is 
compared to the Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve forecasts.
Prieska Copper Zinc Mine Mineral Resources and Reserves 
The Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) reported on in this report contains production targets and 
forecast financial information supported by a combination of Probable Ore Reserves, Indicated 
Mineral Resources and Inferred Mineral Resources, all as defined, compiled and disclosed in 
compliance with ASX Listing Rules and the Australasian Code for Reporting of Exploration Results, 
Mineral Resources and Ore Reserves, 2012 (JORC (2012) or JORC Code) reporting standards. The Ore 
Reserves and Mineral Resources supporting the production target in this report have been prepared by 
Competent Persons in accordance with the requirements in Appendix 5A (JORC (2012)).

  4 Method used to determine Cu equivalent Zn grades:               
   Metal price assumptions based on consensus long-term forecasts (December 2024).
   Method used to determine Cu Equivalent (CuEq) grades is consistent with the formula determined and applied in BFS-20 refer ASX/JSE release 26 2020,
   taking into account current market conditions and NSR currently offered by reputable trading entities.
   1% Zn = (Zn price x Zn NSR) x (Zn plant recovery) = (2,450 x 69.7%) x (82.1%) = 0.185% Cu
     (Cu price x Cu NSR) x (Cu plant recovery) (8,900 x 101.3%) (85.5%)
   Cu Equivalent grade = Cu grade + 0.185 x Zn grade).

--- Section D009.4 | original physical page 32 | text selection | Mixed / unspecified | Jacomynspan Project Mineral Resources ---
The Mineral Resource Estimate for the Jacomynspan Prospect in the Namaqua-Disawell Project is as 
reported in the 2018 Annual Report. There are no material changes to the estimate. 
A maiden Mineral Resource Estimate, based on drilling data from 1971 to 2012, reported at a 
0.4% Ni cut-off grade, gives 6.8Mt of Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources @ 0.57% Ni, 0.33% 
Cu, 0.03% Co, 0.19g/t Pt, 0.12g/t Pd and 0.087g/t Au (refer ASX/JSE release 8 March 2018). 
The Mineral Resources for the Jacomynspan Project were previously reported (refer ASX/JSE 
release 14 July 2016) in accordance with the SAMREC Code (2007) as a “qualifying foreign 
resource estimate” as defined in the ASX Listing Rules. 
The Mineral Resources have subsequently been reassessed by the MSA Group (Pty) Ltd on behalf of 
the Company and reported in compliance with the JORC Code, 20126

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

**Q13 [Medium]: Prieska 31Mt resource and Okiep 10Mt resource | 132kt contained copper — grade, contained metal, reserve vs resource classification, recoveries, reserve conversion.**
- **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
- **Answer & evidence**: Prieska combined Mineral Resource (inclusive of reserves) is 31Mt @ 1.2% Cu / 3.6% Zn = 370kt Cu / 1,120kt Zn, split Indicated 20Mt @ 1.22% Cu / 3.47% Zn (240kt Cu / 690kt Zn) and Inferred 11Mt @ 1.2% Cu / 3.9% Zn (130kt Cu / 420kt Zn) [D009.2, physical PDF p. 30]. Prieska Ore Reserve is 15.6Mt @ 1.1% Cu / 3.1% Zn = 164kt Cu / 458kt Zn (Probable only) [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]. Okiep total Mineral Resource is 11.54Mt (0.44 Measured + 7.20 Indicated + 3.90 Inferred) @ ~1.33% Cu = 152kt Cu (5kt + 98kt + 49kt) [D009.1, physical PDF p. 33] — **not** the 10Mt/132kt figure carried from D008.2. Okiep Ore Reserve is 6.114Mt @ 1.16% Cu = 71.2kt Cu (Probable only) [D009.1, physical PDF p. 33]. Recoveries are only disclosed for Prieska CuEq formula (Cu 85.5%, Zn 82.1%) [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]; Okiep recoveries remain open. Reserve conversion: Prieska 15.6/31.0 = 50% of resource tonnes; Okiep 6.114/11.54 = 53% of resource tonnes. Remainder: Okiep recovery assumptions and the 10Mt/132kt vs 11.54Mt/152kt discrepancy to be resolved in D012.

**Q17 [High]: Prieska study discount rate, Cu/Zn price deck, FX, recovery (capex A$578m and 13.2-yr LOM captured).**
- **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
- **Answer & evidence**: Price deck partially disclosed in the CuEq footnote: Zn US$2,450/t and Cu US$8,900/t, described as "consensus long-term forecasts (December 2024)" [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]. Recoveries: Cu 85.5%, Zn 82.1% (Mintek/DRA test work) [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]. NSR factors: Zn 69.7%, Cu 101.3% [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]. Discount rate and FX rate are **not** disclosed in this section — carry to D012.

**Q18 [High]: Reconcile Prieska LOM 213kt Cu / 611kt Zn to reserve tonnes × grade × recovery.**
- **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote 1 — Deep Sulphide Mineral Resource (Effective Date 18 December 2018)** [D009.2, physical PDF p. 30]
- Source release: ASX/JSE 18 December 2018 "Landmark Resource Upgrade Sets Strong Foundation". Competent Persons: Mr Errol Smart (exploration), Mr Sean Duggan (Mineral Resource).
- Implication: The Deep Sulphide resource is **seven years old** (Dec 2018) and has not been updated despite subsequent drilling. The company confirms "all material assumptions and technical parameters... continue to apply and have not materially changed." For forecasting, this means the 29Mt Deep Sulphide resource is a stale estimate — any resource extension or grade reconciliation in future periods could move it materially. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 whether any impairment or re-estimation trigger exists for the Deep Sulphide resource given its age.

**Footnote 2 — +105 Level Mineral Resource (Effective Date 28 March 2025)** [D009.2, physical PDF p. 30]
- Source releases: oxide zone from 25 July 2023 "Prieska Crown Pillar + 105 Level Mineral Resource increases to 2.3Mt @ 1.7% Cu and 1.6% Zn ahead of Trial Mining"; supergene sulphide and hypogene zones from 28 March 2025 "Prieska Crown Pillar 105 Level Mineral Resource Update". Competent Person: Mr Sean Duggan.
- Implication: The +105 Level resource is current (March 2025) and is the **only** Prieska resource updated in FY26. The oxide zone (0.7Mt @ 0.73% Cu) is a small, low-grade component; the supergene/hypogene zones (1.4Mt @ ~2.7% Cu) are the higher-grade component. The 2.1Mt total at 1.8% Cu is a small fraction of the 31Mt combined resource. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 whether the +105 Level oxide material is included in the LOM schedule and at what recovery (oxide recoveries typically differ from sulphide).

**Footnote 3 — Prieska Ore Reserve (Effective Date 28 March 2025)** [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]
- Source release: ASX/JSE 28 March 2025 "Prieska Feasibility Study Delivers Robust Outcomes". Competent Persons: Mr Ettienne Oosthuizen (Ore Reserve), Ms Vannessa Clark (Ore Reserve).
- **Critical typo**: The footnote states "all material assumptions and technical parameters underpinning the estimates in the ASX/JSE release of **8 March 2025** continue to apply" — but the release is dated **28 March 2025**. This is a one-character typo (8 vs 28) but creates ambiguity about which release underpins the reserve. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 that the correct release date is 28 March 2025 and that no 8 March 2025 release exists.
- Implication: The reserve is current (March 2025) and is the basis for the DFS. The reserve is **Probable only** (no Proved) — a lower-confidence classification that typically carries a higher discount rate in valuation. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the discount rate applied to Probable-only reserves.

**Footnote 4 — CuEq formula** [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]
- Formula: 1% Zn = (Zn price × Zn NSR) × (Zn plant recovery) / (Cu price × Cu NSR) × (Cu plant recovery) = (2,450 × 69.7%) × (82.1%) / (8,900 × 101.3%) × (85.5%) = 0.185% Cu.
- **Arithmetic check**: Numerator = 2,450 × 0.697 × 0.821 = 1,402. Denominator = 8,900 × 1.013 × 0.855 = 7,708. Ratio = 1,402 / 7,708 = 0.182 ≈ 0.185 (rounding). **Checks out.**
- **Critical observation**: The Cu NSR factor is **101.3%** — i.e., the Cu concentrate is assumed to be paid at a **premium** to the Cu price (101.3% of contained Cu). This is unusual (most NSR factors are below 100% due to treatment/refining charges). It implies the Cu concentrate is expected to be sold at a premium, possibly due to low deleterious elements or a specific offtake arrangement. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the offtake terms underpinning the 101.3% Cu NSR — is this a negotiated premium, and is it contracted or assumed?
- **Price deck**: Cu US$8,900/t, Zn US$2,450/t, "consensus long-term forecasts (December 2024)". This is the **reserve** price deck, not necessarily the DFS financial model deck. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 whether the DFS NPV uses the same deck or a different one.

**Footnote 6 — Jacomynspan Mineral Resource (8 March 2018)** [D009.4, physical PDF p. 32]
- Source release: ASX/JSE 8 March 2018 "Modelling confirms targets surrounding Jacomynspan Intrusive". Competent Person: Mr Jeremy Witley (MSA Group).
- Implication: The Jacomynspan resource is **eight years old** (March 2018) and has not been updated. It is a nickel-copper-cobalt-PGM resource (6.8Mt @ 0.57% Ni, 0.33% Cu) — **not** a copper resource. For forecasting, this is a stranded asset with no development pathway disclosed. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the carrying value of the Jacomynspan tenements and whether any impairment indicator exists.

**Footnote 7 — Okiep Mineral Resource (Effective Date 28 March 2025)** [D009.1, physical PDF p. 33]
- Source releases: Jan Coetzee and Nababeep Kloof from 29 March 2021 "Additional Mineral Resource Estimate for the Okiep Copper Prospect, Flat Mines" (Competent Person: Dr Deon Vermaakt); FMN, FMS, FME from 28 August 2023 "Orion upgrades Mineral Resources at the Flat Mines Area, Okiep Copper Project as BFS nears completion" (Competent Person: Mr Sean Duggan); FMNb from 28 March 2025 "Orion Updates Mineral Resources at Okiep Copper Project" (Competent Person: Mr Paul Matthews).
- Implication: The Okiep resource is a **composite of three vintages** (2021, 2023, 2025). The Jan Coetzee and Nababeep Kloof resources are **five years old** (March 2021) and Inferred-only. The FMN/FMS/FME resources are three years old (August 2023). Only FMNb is current (March 2025). **Verification required**: confirm in D012 whether the 2021 and 2023 resources have been re-validated under current modifying factors, and whether the Okiep DFS optimisation (completed FY26 per D008.2) used these stale estimates.

**Okiep Ore Reserve notes** [D009.1, physical PDF p. 33]
- "No Inferred Mineral Resources are included in the Ore Reserve estimate." — confirms the reserve is Measured + Indicated only.
- "Tonnage and grade reported as delivered to the metallurgical plant." — **critical**: the reserve grade (1.16% Cu) is a **delivered** grade, not an in-situ grade. This means mining dilution and recovery factors are already embedded. For forecasting, the 71.2kt Cu reserve contained metal is what arrives at the plant, not what is in the ground. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the in-situ grade and dilution factor to reconcile to the resource grade (1.33% Cu).
- "Measured Mineral Resources at FMN have been converted to Probable Ore Reserves due to insufficient confidence relating to the modifying factors, costs and planning assumptions." — **critical**: 0.44Mt of Measured resource (5kt Cu) has been **downgraded** to Probable reserve. This is unusual (Measured typically converts to Proved) and signals that the company itself has low confidence in the Okiep modifying factors. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the specific modifying factors (costs, planning assumptions) that triggered the downgrade — this is a red flag for the Okiep DFS economics.
- "The proportion of Measured Mineral Resources in the mine plan is approximately 4% by tonnage." — confirms the mine plan is 96% Indicated/Probable, 4% Measured. Low Measured content increases reserve risk.

**Prieska Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve Annual Comparison** [D009.3, physical PDF p. 31]
- All rows show "No material change" for FY26. This confirms **no reserve/resource depletion was booked in FY26** despite the DFS and early works. For forecasting, this means the FY26 production was nil (pre-production) and the reserve is intact at 15.6Mt. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 that no ore was mined in FY26 (trial mining may have occurred — the +105 Level resource was updated "ahead of Trial Mining" in 2023).

**Okiep Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve Annual Comparison** [D009.1, physical PDF p. 33]
- All rows show "No material change" for FY26. Same implication as Prieska — no depletion booked. **Verification required**: confirm in D012 whether any Okiep trial mining or bulk sampling occurred in FY26.

**Jacomynspan Mineral Resource Annual Comparison** [D009.4, physical PDF p. 32]
- All rows show "No material change" for FY26. The table has a **data anomaly**: the "Pd (g/t)" column shows "2.6" for Indicated and "3.8" for Inferred in the Namaqua-Disawell rows, vs "0.1" in the Jacomynspan rows above. This appears to be a **column misalignment** (the 2.6 and 3.8 are likely Co grade or another metal, not Pd). **Verification required**: confirm in D012 the correct Pd grade for Jacomynspan (the standalone table shows 0.11g/t Pd for Indicated and 0.13g/t Pd for Inferred).

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

The following stored questions can be tested, answered, or partially answered using the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position (D010, p. 45). All other stored questions remain open and are carried forward to Section 4.

- **Q44 [Medium] — Shares issued per FY26 raise, resulting share count/options outstanding, diluted count**:
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Issued capital rose from $225,459k (2025) to $258,454k (2026), an increase of **$32,995k** [D010, p. 45]. This confirms a material equity raise during FY26. However, the number of shares issued, issue price, options outstanding, and diluted share count are **not disclosed on the face of the statement** — these require Note 12 (Issued capital) and the share-based payment note. Carry forward to D012.

- **Q46 [Low] — Accounting treatment of IDC convertible loan (debt vs equity), embedded derivative**:
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Loans are presented as a **liability** — current $7,310k (2025: $2,443k) and non-current $23,587k (2025: $32,606k), total $30,897k (2025: $35,049k) [D010, p. 45]. The IDC convertible loan therefore appears to be classified as debt, not equity. However, the split between IDC, Glencore, Triple Flag and other facilities, the embedded derivative treatment, and conversion mechanics are **not disclosed here** — require Note 19 (Loans). Carry forward to D012.

- **Q40 [High] — IDC residual ZAR272.4m loan coupon, repayment, subordination, unsecured status; conversion price/mechanics**:
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: Total loans fell by $4,152k net (from $35,049k to $30,897k) [D010, p. 45], consistent with partial repayment/amortisation during FY26. The specific IDC residual balance, coupon, repayment schedule, subordination, security status and conversion price are **not disclosed on the face of the statement** — require Note 19. Carry forward to D012.

- **Q38 [High] — Glencore US$50m early-works tranche committed vs discretionary; drawn by 30 Jun 2026?**:
  - **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
  - **Answer & evidence**: The statement shows **no separate "borrowings – Glencore" line**; total loans of $30,897k are modest relative to a US$50m (~A$75m+) tranche, and the **non-current loan balance fell** year-on-year [D010, p. 45]. This is consistent with the early-works tranche **not being drawn at 30 June 2026**, but the statement does not name counterparties. Confirm in Note 19 whether any Glencore facility is drawn and the committed/undrawn split. Carry forward to D012.

Critically, **deferred exploration, evaluation and development of $90,939k** (2025: $83,690k) — an increase of **$7,249k** — represents capitalised Prieska/Okiep spend to date, but this is far below the A$578m peak capital requirement. The statement confirms the company is **pre-funding-close** with minimal cash and no large drawn project debt. The precise residual gap still requires the funding note. Carry forward to D012.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

The Consolidated Statement of Financial Position (D010, p. 45) contains **no table footnotes, asterisks, or small-print qualifications** in the supplied evidence. The only embedded qualification is the standard auditor/notes reference:

- **"The notes set out on pages 92 – 132 are an integral part of these consolidated financial statements."** [D010, p. 45]
  - **What it changes**: This confirms that the face of the statement is **not self-sufficient** — every material line item (loans, contract liabilities, deferred exploration, NCI, related-party loans, provisions, rehabilitation bonds) is defined and disaggregated only in Notes 1–20+ on pages 92–132 (which fall within D012, physical PDF pp. 47–67). The page reference "92–132" is a **printed page label**, not a physical PDF page — the physical PDF range for D012 is 47–67, so the printed page numbers are offset by ~45 pages. This is a verification point: confirm the printed-to-physical page mapping when D012 is captured.
  - **Hidden constraint revealed**: The balance sheet shows **cash of only $14,460k** against **total liabilities of $52,930k** and **deferred exploration of $90,939k** — the company is carrying a large capitalised project book funded by a mix of equity ($258,454k issued capital), related-party loans ($6,710k), contract liabilities ($12,813k) and third-party loans ($30,897k). The **funding structure is not closed** (no large drawn project debt), which is the single most consequential forecast caveat: the Prieska A$578m peak capital is **not yet funded** on the balance sheet.
  - **Specific check required in D012**: Note 19 (Loans) must disaggregate the $30,897k by counterparty (IDC, Glencore, Triple Flag, other), state drawn vs undrawn, coupon, security, repayment and CP status. Note 20 (Contract liabilities) must identify the $12,813k counterparty and terms (likely offtake/prepayment). Note 5 (Deferred exploration) must split the $90,939k by project (Prieska vs Okiep vs other) and state the capitalisation policy and any impairment.

- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`) are present** in the supplied table. There is therefore **no missing footnote text** to flag in this section — but the absence of footnotes on a balance sheet of this complexity is itself notable: all disaggregation is deferred to D012.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote/qualification 1 — "The notes set out on pages 92 – 132 are an integral part of these consolidated financial statements."** [D010-ins, p.45]
- **What it changes**: This is a **page-reference anomaly**. The report map states the financial statements run to physical PDF p.67 (D012) and the auditor's report to p.73 (D013), yet this footnote points to **pages 92–132** — which do not exist in a 73-page PDF. This is either a stale template reference from a longer prior-year document, or the physical page numbering differs from printed page labels. **It means the note numbers cited on the face (Notes 5, 21, 22, 23, 25, 26) cannot be located by page reference alone** — they must be found by note number in D012. Verification required: confirm the actual note page range in D012 and whether the "92–132" reference is a printing error.

**Footnote/qualification 2 — OCI arithmetic tension (no footnote, but a face-level qualification).** [D010-ins, p.45]
- The statement shows: Foreign currency reserve **$(1,301)k**; then "Other comprehensive income for the year, net of income tax" **$3,498k**; then "Total other comprehensive income" **$2,197k**.
- **Arithmetic check**: $(1,301)k + $3,498k = **$2,197k** ✓ — the total reconciles. **However**, the line labelled "Other comprehensive income for the year, net of income tax" at $3,498k is **not explained by any preceding line item** — there is no second OCI component (e.g., revaluation, actuarial gain, cash-flow hedge) shown above it. The $(1,301)k FX reserve is the only named component. **This means $3,498k of OCI is unexplained on the face** — either a missing line item (e.g., a fair-value or revaluation reserve movement) or a mislabelled subtotal. This is material: it is larger than the entire loss from continuing operations attributable to owners ($9,516k) at ~37% of it, and it drives the difference between the loss for the year ($12,687k) and total comprehensive loss ($10,490k). **Verification required in D012**: locate the statement of changes in equity / OCI note to identify the $3,498k component. If it is a non-cash revaluation, it should be excluded from forecast cash flow; if it is a mislabelling, the OCI presentation needs correction.

**Footnote/qualification 3 — "Loss from continuing operations" with no discontinued operations line.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- The face labels the result "Loss from continuing operations attributable to equity holders of the Group" but **no discontinued operations line appears anywhere** — implying there were none. This is a qualification worth noting: the entire loss is from continuing operations, so there is no FY25/FY26 discontinued-operations distortion to strip out when building the forecast base. **Verification required in D012**: confirm no discontinued operations note exists (i.e., no disposed subsidiary in FY25 or FY26).

**Footnote/qualification 4 — Income tax expense of nil.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- **Income tax expense = $0** in both FY26 and FY25, despite a pre-tax loss of $(12,687)k. This is consistent with an unrecognised deferred tax asset on accumulated losses (pre-revenue explorer), but it is a **qualification on the forecast**: no tax shield is being recognised, and the company will carry a large accumulated-loss balance into production. **Verification required in D012 (Note 25)**: confirm the unrecognised deferred tax asset amount and the accumulated tax losses available to offset future Prieska/Okiep taxable income — this materially affects post-production cash tax forecasts.

**Footnote/qualification 5 — "Results from operating activities" presentation.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- The face shows "Results from operating activities" of **$(10,903)k** (FY25: $(12,937)k) as a **subtotal placed in the left-hand numeric column**, with the individual expense lines in the right-hand column. This is a **column-presentation qualification**: the operating result is a derived subtotal, not a directly reported line. **Arithmetic check**: Other income $322k − Employee expenses $2,781k − E&E expensed $2,649k − Other operational expenses $5,795k = **$(10,903)k** ✓. The subtotal reconciles. No action beyond noting the presentation.

**Footnote/qualification 6 — Non-operating expenses $(1,330)k vs $(696)k.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- Non-operating expenses **nearly doubled** (+91.1% YoY) to $(1,330)k. No footnote explains the composition. Given the D010 balance-sheet context (deferred exploration +$7,249k, provisions $4,382k, rehab bonds $5,345k), this could include impairment, write-offs, or FX losses. **Verification required in D012 (Note 21)**: obtain the breakdown of non-operating income/(expenses) — if it contains a non-recurring impairment or write-off, it should be excluded from the recurring cost base; if it contains recurring FX losses, it should be forecast.

**Footnote/qualification 7 — Finance income $4,895k vs finance costs $5,349k.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- Finance income of **$4,895k** on a cash balance of only **$14,460k** (per D010 p.45) implies an **effective yield of ~33.8%** — which is implausible for a bank deposit. This is a **material arithmetic/interpretation tension**. Possible explanations: (a) finance income includes interest on loans to related parties ($6,710k per D010 p.45) or other receivables, not just cash; (b) it includes a non-cash accretion or unwinding of discount; (c) the cash balance is an average vs year-end mismatch. **Verification required in D012 (Note 22)**: obtain the composition of finance income — if it is non-cash or one-off, it must be excluded from the forecast; if it is interest on related-party loans, the counterparty and recoverability must be checked (links to Q28).

**Footnote/qualification 8 — Headline loss per share equals basic loss per share.** [D010-ins, p.45]
- **Headline loss per share (0.12) = basic loss per share (0.12)**, and diluted = basic. This implies **no headline adjustments** (no impairment, no loss on disposal added back) — consistent with a clean, pre-revenue cost base. It also confirms **no dilutive instruments are in the money** (options anti-dilutive on a loss). **Verification required in D012 (Note 26)**: confirm the headline earnings reconciliation is nil and obtain the option/warrant count for the diluted-share forecast.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **"The notes set out on pages 92 – 132 are an integral part of these consolidated financial statements."** [D011, physical PDF p. 46]
  - This is the only footnote/qualification on the page. It is a **stale template reference**: the PDF is 73 pages and the notes are in D012 (physical pp. 47–67). It changes nothing about the numbers but confirms the financial statements were assembled from a template without updating cross-references. **Verification**: locate notes by number (Note 5, 11, 19, 20, 21, 22, 25, 26) in D012, not by the printed page range.

- **Direct-method presentation qualification (implicit, not footnoted)**: The operating section is presented on a **direct basis** (receipts/payments), so there are **no non-cash add-backs** (depreciation, impairment, share-based payment, unrealised FX). This means the cash flow statement cannot be used to verify the P&L non-cash items (Q92 OCI $3,498k, Q93 finance income gap, Q103 impairment, Q104 depletion). All must be verified in D012 notes.

- **Two E&E cash lines (operating vs investing)** [D011, p. 46]: Operating E&E payment $(2,366)k vs investing E&E payment $(5,246)k. The operating line's 62× YoY jump (from $38k) alongside a 64% fall in the investing line is a **material classification shift** that changes the interpretation of "E&E expensed" vs "E&E capitalised" in the P&L (Q99). Must be reconciled to Note 5 and the accounting policy in D012.

- **Interest paid/received netted into operating** [D011, p. 46]: Interest paid $(188)k and interest received $115k are inside operating cash flow, not financing/investing. This is an accounting policy choice (IAS 7 allows it) and means "Net cash used in operating activities" $(10,675)k is **not** a clean proxy for EBITDA — it includes net interest. For forecasting, strip out: operating cash burn before net interest = $(10,675)k + $188k − $115k = **$(10,602)k**.

- **"Effect of exchange rate on cash at the end of the year" $194k** [D011, p. 46]: Positive FX effect on cash despite the FCTR swing to $(1,097)k on the balance sheet [D010, p. 45]. The $194k is a cash revaluation gain; the FCTR movement is a translation reserve movement on foreign operations — different items, not contradictory, but worth confirming in the FX note (Q1/Q43).

**Q92 [High]: $3,498k "Other comprehensive income for the year, net of income tax" has no named component above it [D010-ins p.45]. Locate OCI note / statement of changes in equity; identify the $3,498k component.**
- **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012)`
- **Answer & evidence**: The Statement of Changes in Equity [D011-ins, physical PDF p. 46] shows FY26 OCI split into two components: FCTR $(1,301)k and a $3,498k credit posted directly to **Accumulated losses** (not to a named OCI reserve). Total OCI = $2,197k, which reconciles to the face P&L OCI line. The $3,498k is therefore an item taken through OCI but accumulated in retained losses — most plausibly an actuarial gain on post-retirement obligations or a revaluation/IFRS 9-related item. **The nature of the $3,498k remains unidentified**; the statement of changes in equity does not name it. Carry to D012 (OCI note / employee benefits note).
- **Arithmetic check**: $(1,301)k + $3,498k = $2,197k ✓ matches face OCI. FY25 comparative: $(1,174)k + $4,125k = $2,953k ✓.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote: "The notes set out on pages 92 – 132 are an integral part of these consolidated financial statements." [D011-ins, physical PDF p. 46]**
- **What it changes**: Nothing financially — but it is a **confirmed stale cross-reference**. The PDF has 73 physical pages and D012 (Notes) occupies physical pp. 47–67. The "92–132" range is a leftover from a longer-form document or a different pagination convention. This matters for the analyst because any instruction to "see pages 92–132" must be ignored; notes must be located by note number in D012. It also raises a mild **document-control question**: if page references are stale, are there other stale cross-references (e.g., the "8 March 2025" vs "28 March 2025" typo in D009.3, Q79)? Treat printed page references in this report as unreliable.

**Embedded qualification — "Change in ownership" $8,363k (accumulated losses $6,533k + NCI $1,830k) [D011-ins, p. 46]**
- **What it changes**: This is the single largest non-P&L equity movement in FY26 and it is **not explained on the face of the statement**. A credit to accumulated losses of $6,533k and to NCI of $1,830k, with no cash flow, implies either (a) an equity-settled transaction increasing the group's ownership in a subsidiary without loss of control, or (b) a step-acquisition/restructuring. It **inflates total equity by $8,363k** and therefore flatters the equity position relative to the loss for the year. For forecasting, this is a **non-recurring, non-cash equity item** that must be stripped out of any "underlying equity build" or book-value trend. It also interacts with Q102 (NCI %) and Q73/Q90 (Jacomynspan attributable %). **Must be verified in D012** (Note 14 / business combinations / related-party note).

**Embedded qualification — "IFRS 9 capital contribution" $1,315k (other reserve $1,302k + NCI $13k) [D011-ins, p. 46]**
- **What it changes**: A non-cash contribution to equity of $1,315k, up from $432k in FY25. This is an IFRS 9-related equity contribution — typically arising where a financial liability (e.g., a convertible loan or a related-party loan) is settled or modified at a value different from carrying amount, with the difference taken to equity. It **does not flow through P&L** and is **non-cash**. For forecasting, treat as non-recurring. **Must be verified in D012** (financial instruments note / borrowings note) — it may be linked to the IDC convertible loan (Q40, Q46) or the Glencore facility (Q9).

**Embedded qualification — "Transfer of share options expired" $(275)k and "Share options exercised" $(127)k [D011-ins, p. 46]**
- **What it changes**: Confirms the option scheme had both expiries and exercises in FY26. The $(127)k "share options exercised" is a **reserve-to-issued-capital transfer**, not a cash item — the cash ($265k per D011) is already in the $30,319k+$265k proceeds. This reconciles part of the Q109 gap. It also confirms **dilutive instruments were live during FY26**, supporting the need for a diluted share count (Q96, Q97).

**Embedded qualification — "Other comprehensive income/(loss)" split: FCTR $(1,301)k + accumulated losses $3,498k [D011-ins, p. 46]**
- **What it changes**: The $3,498k OCI credit is **accumulated in retained losses, not in a named reserve**. This is unusual presentation and means the OCI item is not separately visible as a reserve on the balance sheet. It also means the FCTR movement $(1,301)k is the only "true" reserve OCI. For forecasting, the $3,498k is a **non-cash, non-recurring OCI item** whose nature (actuarial gain? revaluation?) must be identified before it can be projected. **Must be verified in D012** (OCI note / employee benefits note).

**Arithmetic checks performed on this section:**
- Total comprehensive income FY26: $(9,516)k + $(3,171)k + $(1,301)k + $3,498k = $(10,490)k ✓ matches stated total.
- Closing equity FY26: $258,454k + $22,460k + $(1,097)k + $3,252k + $(147,933)k + $(13,658)k = **$121,478k**. **Stated total is $120,456k — a $1,022k discrepancy.** This is a **material arithmetic tension** and must be flagged. (Re-check: 258,454 + 22,460 = 280,914; −1,097 = 279,817; +3,252 = 283,069; −147,933 = 135,136; −13,658 = **121,478**.) The stated total of $120,456k does not foot. Either a column is mis-transcribed in the capture or the report itself has a footing error. **Flag as a verification question for D012 / re-capture of p. 46.**
- Opening equity FY26: $225,459k + $21,158k + $204k + $1,759k + $(149,745)k + $(12,330)k = **$86,505k**. Stated total is $86,503k — a **$2k rounding difference** (acceptable).
- FY25 closing equity check: $221,200k + $20,855k + $1,376k + $1,907k + $(143,156)k + $(9,243)k = **$92,939k**. Stated $92,940k — $1k rounding (acceptable).
- FY25 total comprehensive income: $(11,864)k + $(3,491)k + $(1,174)k + $4,125k = $(12,404)k ✓ matches stated.
- **The FY26 closing-equity $1,022k discrepancy is the key arithmetic flag from this section.**

Accounting Policies
1. Corporate information
Orion Minerals Limited (Company) is a company domiciled in Australia. The address of the Company’s 
registered office is Level 27, 120 Collins Street, Melbourne, Victoria, 3000. The consolidated financial 
statements as at and for the year ended 30 June 2026 comprised the Company and its subsidiaries, 
(together referred to as the Group). The Group is a for-profit group and is primarily involved in copper, 
zinc, nickel, gold and platinum group elements (PGE) exploration, evaluation and development.
2. Material accounting policies
2.1 Basis of preparation
2.1.1 Statement of compliance
The consolidated financial statements are general purpose financial statements which have been 
prepared in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards (AAS) adopted by the Australian 
Accounting Standards Board (AASB) and the Corporations Act 2001. The consolidated financial 
statements comply with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS®) adopted by the 
International Accounting Standards Board (IASB). The consolidated financial statements were 
authorised for issue by the Board of directors on 17 September 2026. 
2.1.2 Basis of measurement
The consolidated financial statements have been prepared on the historical cost basis except where 
otherwise stated.
The accounting policies set out below have been applied consistently to all periods presented in these 
consolidated financial statements and across the Group, except as required by the new accounting 
standards and interpretations adopted as disclosed in Note 2.2.
2.1.3 Going concern
The financial statements have been prepared on the going concern basis, which contemplates 
continuity of normal business activities and the realisation of assets and discharge of liabilities in the 
normal course of business.
As disclosed in the financial statements the Group recorded a net loss for the year ended 30 June 2026 
of $12.69 million and the Group’s position as at 30 June 2026 was as follows:
• The Group had cash reserves of $14.46 million and had negative operating cash flows of $10.68 
million for the year ended 30 June 2026;
• The Group had positive working capital at 30 June 2026 of $4.68 million; and
• The Group’s main activity is exploration, evaluation and development of base metal, gold and PGE 
projects in South Africa (Northern Cape) and as such it does not have a source of income, rather it is 
reliant on debt and/or equity raisings to fund its activities.
These factors indicate a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt as to whether the Group 
will continue as a going concern and therefore whether it will realise its assets and extinguish its 
liabilities in the normal course of business and at the amounts stated in the financial report.
Cash on hand as at 30 June 2026 will not be sufficient to fund planned exploration and operational 
activities during the next twelve months. Further capital raising will need to take place in Q4 of 
FY2027. However, the Directors believe that there are reasonable grounds that the Group will be able 
to continue as a going concern, after consideration of the following factors:
(i) Project funding - Prieska Copper Zinc Mine
Triple Flag US $87M Funding Package
In December 2022, Orion signed definitive agreements with Triple Flag Precious Metals Corp. (TSX/
NYSE: TFPM) (with its subsidiaries, Triple Flag) for a US$87 million (~$127 million) secured funding 
package for PCZM comprising of a precious metals stream (Precious Metal Stream) and an additional 
early funding arrangement (Funding Arrangement).

The Precious Metal Stream, still available to Orion, is conditional on the mine development being fully

(ii) Binding financing and offtake agreement
In February 2026 Orion’s subsidiary - Prieska Copper Zinc Mine (Pty) Ltd (PCZM) - executed a binding

Orion Minerals Ltd will be guarantor for obligations of PCZM under the facility.

In February 2026, Orion was selected to participate in the 2026 BHP Xplor accelerator program 
(Program). As part of the Program, Orion received aggregate equity-free grant of US$500K (~$718K) 
in conjunction with access to BHP’s technical specialists and structured support to advance Orion’s 
geological concepts in its Northern Cape exploration projects. A number of Orion’s subsidiaries 
benefitted from the Program.

• The positive impact of the IDC’s conversion of its shareholder loan into equity. The conversion

• The Company’s ability to successfully raise capital in the past, the Directors are confident of 
obtaining the continued support of the Company’s shareholders and a number of brokers that have 
supported the Company’s previous capital raisings.

concern basis as in the opinion of the Directors, the Group will be in a position to continue to meet its

for at least twelve months from the date of this report.

by the Australian Accounting Standards Board (AASB) that are mandatory for the current reporting 
period. Standards which are not yet effective, are being considered by the Group for any impact it
