### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote 1 — Note 10 Prepayments Prospecting Rights [D012.4, p. 55]**
- **Text**: Settlement on 19 March 2026 of the remaining Okiep Copper Project phase with SAFTA, BCC and NCC; cash and share settlement; acquisition of prospecting right in NOM and transfer of remaining rights to NOE; rights to be reclassified to exploration rights once transfer of ownership completed. Second paragraph references a BCC/NCC agreement of ~31 July 2021 (amended 16 April 2024 and 7 May 2024) to acquire prospecting rights "to the value of $2.21 million."
- **What it changes**: The $2,035k non-current prepayment is a *pending-transfer* asset, not yet an exploration right — so it sits outside the $90,939k deferred E&E and $6,809k exploration rights balances. It will reclassify on completion of title transfer, which is a future event with timing risk. The $2.21m agreement value vs $2,035k carrying value vs the $4.14m SAFTA cession noted in D012.2 p.53 creates a three-way reconciliation gap that must be resolved. The 19 March 2026 settlement date coincides with the "Placement – OCP Shareholders (19 March 2026)" of 71,911,941 shares at $0.015 ($1,079k) in Note 12.1 — confirming part of the consideration was scrip.
- **Must verify**: (i) completion date of prospecting right transfer to NOM/NOE; (ii) reconciliation of $2.21m / $2,035k / $4.14m; (iii) whether any of the $2,035k is at risk of impairment if transfer fails.

**Note 11.1 footnote — Ring-fenced cash and facilities [D012.4, p. 55]**
- **Text**: Within cash and cash equivalents is ring-fenced NOM funding ZAR2.4m ($209k) and BHP Xplor $411k, used exclusively for NOM exploration and BHP Xplor respectively. SA subsidiaries have available facilities at RMB: ZAR25m ($2.2m) forex settlement, ZAR5m ($0.44m) guarantee facility, ZAR2.5m ($0.22m) FEC settlement.
- **What it changes**: Of the $14,460k reported cash + deposits, at least $620k is restricted/ring-fenced and not freely available for general corporate or Prieska funding. This is *in addition to* the $5,345k rehabilitation bonds (Q91) — so true unrestricted liquidity is materially lower than the headline $14,460k. The implied FX rate in the facility disclosures (ZAR25m = $2.2m → ~11.36; ZAR5m = $0.44m → ~11.36; ZAR2.5m = $0.22m → ~11.36) is internally consistent at ~11.36 ZAR per *reporting unit*, but if the reporting unit is AUD this is implausible (AUD/ZAR ~11–12 is plausible; USD/ZAR ~18 is not). This suggests the $ figures are AUD-converted at ~11.36 ZAR/AUD — consistent with AUD presentation. Must confirm the rate and date in Note 29.
- **Must verify**: (i) whether the $5,345k rehabilitation bonds are inside or outside the $14,460k; (ii) the FX rate/date used for the ZAR facility conversions; (iii) drawn vs undrawn status of the three RMB facilities.

**Note 11.2 — Reconciliation of net cash used in operating activities [D012.4, p. 55]**
- **Key observations**: Net loss $(12,687)k; add-backs include depreciation $830k, share-based payment $1,895k, gain on FX $(1,687)k, finance income $(4,895)k, finance expense $5,349k, interest received $115k, interest paid $(188)k. Net cash used in operating activities $(10,675)k vs $(7,881)k prior year — a 35% deterioration.
- **What it changes**: The $(1,687)k FX gain add-back is large relative to the $(12,687)k net loss and confirms material FX volatility in the P&L (consistent with D012.2/D012.3 FX gains on PP&E, exploration rights, deferred E&E, preference shares). Finance income $(4,895)k ≈ the preference share interest receivable of $4,894k noted in D012.3 — confirming that the entire finance income line is non-cash accrued preference share interest, not cash interest. This is critical: the company's "finance income" is an accrual on a related-party instrument, not liquidity.
- **Must verify**: (i) confirm finance income $4,895k = preference share interest accrual (ties to Q89); (ii) the $1,687k FX gain — which balance sheet items drove it (ties to Q1/Q43); (iii) why interest paid $(188)k is so low relative to finance expense $5,349k — implying ~$5,161k of finance expense is non-cash (accrued/amortised), which must be confirmed in Note 13/Note 19.

**Note 12.1 — Issued capital [D012.4, p. 56]**
- **Key observations**: 2,103,932,543 net new shares issued in FY26. Gross proceeds ~$34,014k; issue costs $1,019k; net ~$32,995k. Closing issued capital $258,454k. Share count 8,954,380,361.
- **What it changes**: The FY26 equity raise is larger than the A$29.13m previously referenced (Q23). At ~0.65–0.68 AUD/USD, $34.0m gross ≈ A$50–52m — materially above A$29.13m. Either the A$29.13m figure excluded some tranches (e.g., the OCP shareholder scrip-for-asset placement, which is non-cash), or there is a currency/reporting mismatch. The OCP placement ($1,079k) was consideration for the SAFTA/BCC/NCC settlement, not cash raised — so cash equity raised ≈ $32,935k gross ≈ A$48–50m. Still above A$29.13m. Must reconcile (see Q97).
- **Must verify**: (i) reconcile FY26 cash equity raised (~$32.9m) to the A$29.13m figure in D012.1; (ii) confirm which placements were cash vs scrip-for-assets; (iii) post-year-end share count for per-share metrics.

**Note 12.2 — Share-based payments reserve [D012.4, p. 56]**
- **Key observations**: Opening $1,759k; FY26 expense $1,895k; options exercised $(127)k; expired options transferred to accumulated losses $(275)k; closing $3,252k. Footnote 1 confirms expired vested options are transferred to accumulated losses.
- **What it changes**: The $1,895k SBP expense is non-cash and ties to the Note 11.2 add-back. The $(127)k on exercise vs $265k cash received from option exercises (8m @ $0.023 + 3m @ $0.027 + 1m @ $0.023 = $184k + $81k + $23k = $288k) implies a small gain/transfer difference — minor.
- **Must verify**: confirm no further large option tranches vesting in FY27 that would increase non-cash SBP expense.

**Note 12.3 — Options expired [D012.4, p. 56]**
- **Key observations**: 27,000,000 unlisted options expired 15/04/2026 across three classes ($0.023, $0.027, $0.032). Note that 12,000,000 of these (8m + 3m + 1m) were exercised in Feb/May 2026 *before* expiry — so the 27m expired are the residual.
- **What it changes**: Confirms the option overhang is being cleaned up; no dilution from these. But the $0.032 class expiring worthless signals the share price was below $0.032 through April 2026 — consistent with the $0.022 June 2026 placement price.
- **Must verify**: remaining unlisted option balance and exercise prices for FY27 dilution modelling (Note 12 / remuneration note).

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Note 13 fn ¹ — "IFRS 9 loan adjustment $1,302k (2025: $303k); Refer Note 19"** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - This is a **non-cash fair-value adjustment routed through other reserves (equity), not P&L**. It grew 4.3× YoY ($303k → $1,302k), implying a growing fair-value discount being recognised on a loan instrument — most plausibly the IDC convertible loan (fair-value discount to capital contribution per D012.1 p. 50) or the Triple Flag US$10m Funding Arrangement contract liability. **Implication**: the $1,302k is a balance-sheet/equity item, so it does **not** flow through the $5,349k finance expense (Q103) — but the *amortisation* of that discount likely does. Must verify in Note 19 which instrument and whether the unwinding sits in finance costs.

- **Note 14 fn ² — IDC conversion 27 Feb 2026, 23.83% of PCZM Holdco ceded** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - **This is the single most consequential disclosure on the page.** It confirms the IDC convertible loan **converted to equity during FY26**, diluting Orion's PCZM Holdco stake to 76.17%. This changes the interpretation of:
    1. **NCI step-up**: PCZM operating entities NCI rose from 20% → 36.68%; PCZM Holdco from 0% → 23.83%. Future profit/loss attributable to NCI is materially higher — critical for FY27 EPS/attribution forecasts.
    2. **Funding gap (Q23/Q50)**: if IDC converted to equity, the "IDC residual ZAR272.4m loan" may no longer be a debt source — it may now be equity already issued. The A$578m funding stack must be re-based: is IDC now *equity in* rather than *debt to draw*? Must verify in Note 19.
    3. **Q40 conversion mechanics**: conversion price and share count still not stated — must check Note 19.

- **Note 14 fn ¹ — prior-year NOE/NOM cessions** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - Confirms the 2025 NCI movements (15.33% NOE, 5.62% NOM) were Orion cessions, not new capital. Explains the 2025 "partial disposal of subsidiary $276k" line. No forward impact beyond confirming the BEE/partner structure.

- **Note 14 — NCI summarised balance sheets** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - **Prieska Copper Zinc Mine (Pty) Ltd**: loss before tax $(12,541)k; total assets $89,012k; total liabilities $(127,337)k → **net liability position of $(38,325)k**. Non-current liabilities $(126,115)k dominate — this is where the Glencore/Triple Flag/IDC debt sits at the PCZM level. **Implication**: PCZM is balance-sheet insolvent on a standalone basis; the parent guarantee (D012.1 p. 47) and future funding are what keep it a going concern. Critical for going-concern and debt-covenant forecasting.
  - **New Okiep Mining Company (Pty) Ltd**: loss $(2,488)k; current liabilities $(8,741)k vs current assets $376k → **working-capital deficit $(8,365)k**. Relevant to Q94 (JV partner loan recoverability) and Okiep funding needs.

- **Note 15 fn ¹ — Rehabilitation provision offset by Centriq guarantees $5.12m (2025: $4.29m)** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - The provision itself is only **$3,952k** (non-current), yet the Centriq guarantee is **$5.12m** — the guarantee **exceeds the provision by ~$1.17m**. This is a different number from the $5,345k "rehabilitation bonds" in Note 8 (Q91). **Implication**: there may be two distinct instruments (a Centriq insurance guarantee of $5.12m and a separate $5,345k restricted cash/bond), or a reclassification. Must reconcile in D010/D011 and Note 8. Also note the guarantee grew $0.83m YoY while the provision *fell* $131k — a divergence worth flagging.

- **Note 15 fn ² — OCP Transaction Developmental Activities commitment $0.7m (ZAR 8m)** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - A **new quantified commitment**: minimum $0.3m (ZAR 4m) per Target Entity × 2 entities = $0.7m. Cross-referenced to Note 24. **Implication**: this is a contractual exploration spend obligation (not yet provided as a liability — the contractual provision line went to nil). Must confirm in Note 24 whether this is a capital commitment (E&E) or expensed, and the deadline.

- **Note 15 — Provisions reconciliation** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - **"Provisions unused and reversed $(1,184)k"** — a large reversal (vs nil in 2025). The contractual provisions line fell from $684k to nil. **Implication**: a $1,184k credit likely flowed through P&L in FY26 (or reduced cost) — a one-off that flatters FY26 earnings and should be **excluded from run-rate forecasts**. Must confirm in Note 5/Note 20 where the reversal was recognised.

- **Note 16 — Trade and other payables** [D012.5, p. 57]:
  - Trade payables fell $333k to $1,050k; other payables rose $887k to $1,217k. Total payables only $2,267k — **very low for a company with $89m of PCZM assets**, consistent with a pre-development, contractor-light phase. **Implication**: no large accrued capex or contractor liabilities at year-end — supports the "early works only" capex picture (Q31). The $887k rise in other payables should be checked against accruals ($470k per Note 11.2, Q106).

- **Note 17.2 footnote ¹ [D012.6, physical PDF p. 58]**: States that ROU depreciation of ZAR0.85m (~$74k) and lease interest of ZAR1.82m (~$159k) are included in the consolidated statement of profit or loss. **Implication**: (a) confirms lease interest is a real, recurring P&L line (~$159k/yr) that must be modelled separately from debt interest; (b) the ZAR/USD implied rates (~11.45–11.49) corroborate USD as the reporting currency and provide a cross-check for Note 29; (c) the near-flat ROU depreciation ($74k vs $72k) despite the Prieska housing build signals the housing asset is **not yet commissioned** — a FY27 depreciation step-up risk remains unquantified.

- **Note 17.1 structure [D012.6, physical PDF p. 57]**: Lease liabilities are 99.7% non-current ($1,784k of $1,790k) with only $6k current. **Implication**: near-term cash lease repayments are trivial (~$136k/yr total per the repayment line), so leases are not a liquidity constraint; but the long-dated non-current balance implies a multi-year lease (likely land/buildings) whose term and escalation are not disclosed — verify in Note 19/commitments.

Mora Plase
On 22 December 2023, New Okiep Mining Company (Pty) Ltd signed an agreement with Mora Plase (Pty)
Ltd to acquire the property and access right where the New Okiep Mining Company (Pty) Ltd’s mining
operations are being performed. The Purchase consideration to be paid is ZAR36.5 million
(~$3.0 million) of which ZAR14.6 million (~$1.2 million) was paid in January 2024, ZAR7.3 million
(~$0.69 million) paid in January 2025 and ZAR7.3 million (~$0.66 million) was paid in January 2026. The
remaining purchase consideration to be paid on the third anniversary of the initial payment date.
Interest shall accrue annually and compound monthly on the outstanding amount of the purchase price
at Prime Rate plus 2%. Interest payments shall be made bi-annually, starting 6 months after the initial
payment date. Interest paid during the period was ZAR 1.6 million (~$0.15 million).

Current
IDC Shareholder Loan & Landmark Shareholder Loan – Okiep Copper Project
In November 2022, Orion and the Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC)
entered into definitive agreements in terms of which the IDC acquired 43.75% of the issued ordinary
shares in New Okiep Mining Company Proprietary Limited (NOM) and triggered pre-development funding
arrangements for the Flat Mines SAFTA area (Flat Mines Project), refer ASX/JSE release 7 September
2022.
As at 30 June 2026, the IDC has advanced ZAR 78.33 million to NOM to fund the pre-development
expenditure. On 5 February 2025, Orion concluded a BEE transaction with the IDC. Under the terms of
the updated NOM MOI, the transaction resulted in the IDC ceding 22.22% of its shareholding in NOM
to Landmark Capital (BEE Entrepreneur). As a result, a portion of the loan balance due to IDC (ZAR
39.79 million (~$3.4 million)) was ceded to Landmark Capital. The loan with Landmark Capital will be
accounted for in accordance with IFRS 9. The loan is discounted at the South African prime lending rate.
Total loan as at 30 June 2026 before IFRS 9 from Landmark is ZAR39.79 million (~$3.5 million) and from
the IDC is ZAR47.65 million (~$4.2 million). Interest on both the IDC and Landmark loans recognised in
the current period amounted to ZAR 7.73 million ($0.7 million). As part of the initial recognition of the
drawdowns received during the year, ZAR 0.54 million ($0.05 million) was recognised to Other Reserve of
which ZAR 0.2 million ($0.02 million) relates to noncontrolling interest.

 Non-current                                                      
 IDC Shareholder Loan – PCZM Holdco                               
 On 27 February 2026, the Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC), exercised
 their right to convert a portion of the convertible loan with the group’s subsidiaries, PCZM Holdco
 Proprietary Limited (PCZM Holdco) to equity. The conversion was in accordance with the loan facility
 agreement dated February 2023 (Facility Agreement) and the implementation agreement executed.
                                                                  
 Following the equity conversion, the IDC will hold a shareholding of approximately 23.80% in PCZM
 Holdco (16.70% effective shareholding in Prieska Copper Zinc Mine Proprietary Limited (PCZM)).
 Subsequent to the conversion, the IDC ceases being a secured lender and becomes and shareholder. The
 remaining unconverted portion of the loan will become a shareholder loan valued at ZAR 272.4 million
 (~$24 million). The shareholder loan will be accounted for in accordance with IFRS 9 and discounted at
 the South African prime lending rate.                            
 The total loan as at 30 June 2026 before IFRS 9 is ZAR 272.4 million (~$24 million). Interest incurred
 and recognised for the current period amounted to ZAR 9.2 million ($0.8 million). As part of the initial
 recognition of the shareholder loan, ZAR 13.8 million (~$1.2 million) was recognised as a day one gain on
 the extinguishment of the original loan as result of the conversion, ZAR 0.2 million (~$0) was recognised
 to Other Reserve of which ZAR 0.04 million (~$0) was related to non-controlling interest.

   Contract liability - GRR                      12,813   11,611        
                                                                        
                                                                        
  The Group entered into a Gross Revenue Return (GRR) arrangement with TF R&S Canada Limited
  (Triple Flag). In terms of the agreement, the Group is to receive an advance payment of $9.24 million
  ($10 million net of $0.76 million transaction costs) to complete the Feasibility Study for the mining
  of the crown and remnant pillars down to the 385m level at Prieska Copper Zinc Mine (PCZM) and
  the simultaneous commissioning and operating of pumping and water treatment facilities, to allow
  dewatering of the PCZM mine.                                          
  It is determined that the advance payment received comprises of a disposal of a portion of the Group’s
  mineral interest and an upfront payment received implicit to the obligation of future extraction services
  that will generate future gross revenue returns. Once PCZM generates revenue the company will be
  obligated to pay 0.8% of its gross revenue to Triple Flag.            
                                                                        
  It is the intention of the Group to satisfy the performance obligation under the arrangement. The
  obligation will be satisfied through the Group’s production and revenue, which will be recognised over
  the duration of the LOM as the Group delivers the gross revenue return. As the contract is long term in
  nature, and the Group received a portion of the consideration from Triple Flag at inception of the contract.
  It has been determined that a portion of the future extraction contains a significant financing component.
                                                                        
  The contract liability will be recognised as a non-current liability until such time as when the Group starts
  extraction services and the obligation to repay 0.8% of its revenue is incurred.
  As at reporting date, a total of AUD10 million has been received by the Group from Triple Flag in relation
  to the gross revenue agreement. AUD 0.03 million was received on 11 September 2024.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Note 18 — Mora Plase instalment sale (no footnote markers, but embedded qualifications):**
- **Qualification**: "The transaction triggered possible implications of IFRS 16. Upon further assessment, the Group concluded that the transaction was an instalment sale agreement in terms of IFRS 16" [D012.7, p. 58].
- **What it changes**: The Mora Plase property acquisition is not a simple prepayment/asset purchase — it is a financing arrangement. The land is recognised as PP&E with a corresponding instalment sale liability unwound over the term. This means: (i) the $781k current liability is a financing cash outflow in FY27, not capex; (ii) interest accrues at Prime + 2% compounding monthly — a ZAR-denominated floating-rate exposure not captured in the USD debt stack; (iii) the remaining purchase consideration is payable on the third anniversary of the initial payment date (i.e., January 2027), so FY27 sees the final ~ZAR7.3m (~$0.66m) payment plus accrued interest.
- **Verification required**: Confirm the exact third-anniversary payment date and amount in Note 19 continuation or Note 20 commitments; confirm whether the land is included in the PCZM PP&E pledged to Triple Flag (Q92).

**Note 19.1 — IDC/Landmark NOM loans (embedded qualifications):**
- **Qualification**: "The loan with Landmark Capital will be accounted for in accordance with IFRS 9. The loan is discounted at the South African prime lending rate" [D012.7, p. 58].
- **What it changes**: The carrying values ($3,326k Landmark, $3,984k IDC) are IFRS 9-discounted, not face value. Face values are ZAR39.79m (~$3.5m) and ZAR47.65m (~$4.2m) respectively — so the discount is modest (~$0.4m combined). The ZAR0.54m ($0.05m) Other Reserve adjustment on initial recognition is small but confirms the loans were drawn during FY26 (new additions), consistent with the collapse in deferred E&E spend (Q90) — i.e., NOM pre-development was funded by IDC/Landmark drawdowns rather than equity.
- **Verification required**: Confirm whether further IDC/Landmark drawdowns are committed for FY27 (Okiep optimisation funding) — Note 19 continuation / Note 20.

**Note 19.2 — IDC PCZM Holdco conversion (embedded qualifications):**
- **Qualification**: "Subsequent to the conversion, the IDC ceases being a secured lender and becomes a shareholder. The remaining unconverted portion of the loan will become a shareholder loan valued at ZAR 272.4 million (~$24 million)... discounted at the South African prime lending rate" [D012.7, p. 59].
- **What it changes**: This is the single most consequential item in this section for the funding stack. The IDC convertible loan ($26,902k at 30 Jun 2025) has been split: a portion converted to equity (IDC now ~23.80% PCZM Holdco / 16.70% effective PCZM), and the residual ZAR272.4m (~$24m) reclassified from secured convertible debt to unsecured shareholder loan. Implications: (i) the secured debt stack is reduced by the converted portion — improving senior lender positioning for Glencore/Triple Flag; (ii) the residual $24m is now subordinated shareholder debt, prime-linked, IFRS 9 — a cheaper-looking but structurally junior claim; (iii) the ZAR13.8m (~$1.2m) day-one gain on extinguishment is a non-cash P&L credit that flatters FY26 finance costs — must be stripped out of run-rate; (iv) the 23.80% vs 23.83% discrepancy (Q107/Q113) needs reconciliation.
- **Verification required**: Confirm conversion price and shares issued (Q107); confirm whether the residual shareholder loan has a repayment date or is perpetual (Note 19 continuation); confirm the day-one gain's P&L line (finance income vs other income) — Note 19 continuation / D010-ins.

**Note 20 — Triple Flag GRR (embedded qualifications):**
- **Qualification**: "It is determined that the advance payment received comprises of a disposal of a portion of the Group's mineral interest and an upfront payment received implicit to the obligation of future extraction services... Once PCZM generates revenue the company will be obligated to pay 0.8% of its gross revenue to Triple Flag... a portion of the future extraction contains a significant financing component" [D012.7, p. 59].
- **What it changes**: The Triple Flag arrangement is not debt — it is a hybrid: part mineral interest disposal (no liability), part prepaid revenue obligation (contract liability). The $12,813k non-current contract liability will be unwound against revenue over LOM once production starts, meaning: (i) FY27+ revenue will be reduced by 0.8% GRR — a permanent 80bp revenue haircut to model; (ii) the contract liability amortisation is non-cash and will run through revenue, not finance costs; (iii) the "significant financing component" means a portion of the 0.8% is effectively interest — but it is embedded in the revenue line, complicating AISC/unit-cost calculations (Q11). The AUD10m received to date (AUD0.03m on 11 Sep 2024) suggests the bulk was received at/near inception — confirm timing.
- **Verification required**: Confirm the split between mineral interest disposal (equity/PP&E credit) and contract liability at inception; confirm the 0.8% GRR commencement trigger (first revenue vs first concentrate); confirm whether the GRR is deductible for AISC purposes — Note 19 continuation / Note 20 continuation / D008.1.

**Note 20 — arithmetic check:**
- Contract liability GRR: 2026 $12,813k vs 2025 $11,611k — increase of $1,202k. This is likely the significant financing component (unwinding of discount) accreted during FY26, since no new Triple Flag cash was received (only AUD0.03m in Sep 2024). Implied accretion rate ~10.4% on opening balance — plausible for a project-finance discount rate. Flag: confirm the discount rate used and whether accretion runs through finance costs or revenue — Note 19 continuation / Note 20 continuation.

 24. Commitments and contingencies                                       
                                                                         
 Tenement commitments - South Africa and Australia                       
 The Group has a portfolio of tenements located in South Africa and Victoria, Australia, which all have a
 requirement for a certain level of expenditure each and every year in addition to annual rental payments
 for the tenements.                                                      
 Guarantees                                                              
 The Group has the following contingent liabilities at 30 June 2026:     
                                                                         
 • It has negotiated bank guarantees in favour of the South African Government towards obligations of
   mining and exploration tenements. The total of these guarantees at 30 June 2026 was $5.12 million
   (2025: $4.30 million);                                                
 • The Group also has bank guarantees in favour of the Victorian Government for rehabilitation
   obligations and the total of these guarantees at 30 June 2026 was $0.22 million (2025: $0.22 million).
   The Group has sufficient term deposits to cover the outstanding guarantees;
 • Prieska Copper Zinc Mine (Pty) Ltd (PCZM), has a guarantee with Eskom for $0.6 million (2025: nil) in
   relation to prospective mining activities; and                        
 • It has guaranteed to cover the directors and officers in the event of legal claim against the individual
   or as a group for conduct which is within the Company guidelines, operations and procedures.
 As part of the Group’s environmental policy exploration and access sites are regenerated to match
 or exceed local government and state government expectations. The costs are not considered to be
 material by the Group however this policy will be reviewed as exploration and development activities
 increase as the Company moves closer towards commercial production.     
                                                                         
                                                                         
 Project Commitment - Okiep Copper Project                               
 As part of the OCP Transaction the Selling Shareholders are entitled to an agterskot. The Agterskot
 will be calculated on the basis of the number of tonnes of Mineral Resources published on the ASX by
 Orion Minerals in relation the SAFTA Mineral Projects in compliance with the JORC Code less the tonnes
 of the baseline JORC Code Mineral Resource. The maximum Agterskot value payable to the Selling
 Shareholders are ZAR97.05 million (~$8.5 million).                      
 In accordance with the OCP Transaction agreement, the Purchasers (New Okiep Exploration Company
 (Pty) Ltd (NOE) and New Okiep Mining Company (Pty) Ltd (NOM)) would incur developmental expenditure
 in exploring and developing the mineral projects of each Target Entity (SAFTA, NCC and BCC) to satisfy
 the mineralisation requirements. As at 30 June 2026, NOM had incurred its portion of the expenditure,
 while NOE had remaining expenditure of ZAR 2.98 million (~$0.27 million).
                                                                         
 New Okiep Mining Company - Unlawful Occupancy                           
 In the current financial year, New Okiep Mining Company (Py) Ltd (NOM) has commenced evictions of
 the two individuals who occupied land over which NOM has surface rights and will hold the property
 right once ownership is transferred as part of the Mora Plase Instalment sale. The occupiers, to date,

 part of the SAFTA BEE transaction. The preference share is cumulative, redeemable preference share

 to declare dividends to the IDC, however as NOM is currently still in exploration phase and not producing

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

**Footnote ¹ — Note 21.1 Other Income [D012.8, p. 59]**
- **Text**: "Other income relates to the BHP Xplor Accelerator Program... aggregated equity-free grant together with access to BHP's technical specialists. Subsidiary entities... Bartotrax, Masiqhame Trading 855, Orion Exploration No 5/1/4, New Okiep Exploration Company. Joint venture entities... Namaqua Nickel Mining and Disawell."
- **What it changes**: The $260k "Other income" (2025: nil) is a **one-off, non-recurring grant**, not operating revenue. It must be **stripped from FY26 run-rate** for forecasting. It also confirms BHP Xplor funding flows through *multiple* subsidiary and JV entities (not just the parent), which matters for segment/NCI allocation and for Q68 (BHP-funded vs Orion-funded split). The grant is "equity-free" — no dilution, no repayment obligation.
- **Verification required**: Confirm in Note 5 / D008.3 whether any BHP Xplor grant remains unamortised/deferred, and whether FY27 expects further tranches.

**Note 21.2 — Other operational expenses [D012.8, p. 59]**
- **No footnote markers**, but the line-item detail is forecast-relevant: **Contractors, consultants and advisory $3,545k** (up 45% YoY from $2,439k) is the dominant cost and likely contains development-study/DFS/Okiep-optimisation spend that may or may not recur. **Share-based payments $1,895k** (in 21.3, up 94% from $977k) is non-cash and should be added back in cash-flow forecasting but is a real dilution cost. **Depreciation $756k + IFRS 16 $74k** are non-cash.
- **Verification required**: Split contractors/consultants between recurring corporate and one-off project/study costs — Note 5 / D008.

**Note 21.3 — Non-operating income/(expenses) [D012.8, p. 59]**
- **No footnote**, but critical one-offs to strip: **Net FX gain $421k** (volatile, not forecastable as recurring), **Share options exercised $127k** (one-off), **Share-based payments $(1,895)k** (non-cash), **Loss on loan modification IFRS 9 nil in FY26** (FY25 $(143)k). The **$(1,330)k total non-operating expense** is largely non-cash/share-based and should be normalised.

**Note 22 — Finance income [D012.8, p. 59]**
- **Qualification**: Labelled **"Interest received"** — see Q102 contradiction above. This is the single most important classification issue in this section: if genuinely received in cash, the preference-share accrual narrative (Q89) is wrong; if accrued, the label is misleading. **Must verify against D011 cash-flow "interest received" line.**

**Note 23 — Finance costs [D012.8, p. 59]**
- **No footnote**, but the decomposition (Finance expenses $5,044k / Lease $159k / Instalment $146k) resolves the lease and instalment components (Q119) and isolates the $5,044k residual bucket (Q103).

**Note 24 — Commitments and contingencies [D012.8, p. 60]**
- **Agterskot qualification**: "calculated on the basis of the number of tonnes of Mineral Resources published on the ASX... less the tonnes of the baseline JORC Code Mineral Resource. The maximum Agterskot value payable... ZAR97.05 million (~$8.5 million)." This is a **contingent earn-out** tied to resource growth at SAFTA. It is *not* a fixed liability but a real future cash call if Orion publishes additional SAFTA resources. **Must be modelled as a contingent outflow** and checked against D009 SAFTA resource tonnes.
- **OCP developmental expenditure qualification**: "As at 30 June 2026, NOM had incurred its portion of the expenditure, while NOE had remaining expenditure of ZAR 2.98 million (~$0.27 million)." This **revises** the earlier $0.7m (ZAR8m) figure — the remaining obligation is now **$0.27m**, materially lower. NOM's portion is fully incurred.
- **Area Metals preference share qualification**: "cumulative, redeemable preference share of no-par value and is **not convertible** into ordinary shares. Dividends... dependent on NOM declaring dividends... NOM is currently still in exploration phase and not producing concentrate... financial impact is currently uncertain. Management is currently in discussions with funders... timing of when the project will be fully funded is also uncertain." This is a **material clarification**: the IDC preference share in AMH6 is **NOT convertible** (unlike the PCZM Holdco IDC instrument in Q107/Q121) and dividends are contingent on NOM profitability. It confirms **NOM/Okiep is not yet funded** — ties directly to Q65 (Okiep optimisation pending) and Q114 (NOM current liabilities $8,741k vs current assets $376k). The "discussions with funders" language signals an **unresolved Okiep funding gap**.
- **Unlawful occupancy**: up to ZAR0.1m (~$0.008m) — immaterial but confirms Mora Plase ownership transfer is still pending (ties Q124 instalment sale).

   No income tax is payable by the Group. The directors have considered it prudent not to bring to account
   the future income tax benefit of income tax losses and exploration deductions until it is probable that
   future taxable profits will be available against which the unused tax losses can be utilised.
   The Group has estimated un-recouped gross Australian income tax losses of approximately $32.19
   million (2025: $31.07 million) which may be available to offset against taxable income in future years,
   subject to continuing to meet relevant statutory tests.            
                                                                      
   The Group also has carry forward tax losses in South Africa of approximately ZAR32.57 million (~$2.85
   million) (2025: ~$2.7 million) and unredeemed capital expenditure carried forward, which can be offset
   against future mining income, of ZAR1,475 million (~$128.7 million) (2025: ~$114 million).
                                                                      
   Benefits from the Group’s carry forward tax losses will only be obtained if:
                                                                      
   • the Group derives future assessable income of a nature and an amount sufficient to enable the benefit
     from the deductions for the loss to be realised;                 
   • the Group continues to comply with the conditions for deductibility imposed by tax legislation; and
   • no changes in taxation legislation adversely affect the economic entity in realising the benefit from
     the deductions for the losses.                                   
   Except to the extent that it does not offset a net deferred tax liability, a deferred tax asset has not been
   recognised in the accounts for these unused losses because it is not probable that future taxable profit
   will be available to use against such losses.                      
                                                                      
   Tax consolidation                                                  
   For the purposes of Australian income taxation, the Company and its 100% controlled Australian
   subsidiaries have formed a tax consolidation group. The parent entity, Orion Minerals Ltd, reports to the
   Australian Taxation Office on behalf of all the Australian entities.

26. Loss per share
Basic loss per share amounts are calculated by dividing the net loss for the year attributable to
ordinary equity holders of the parent by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding
during the year.
Diluted earnings per share amounts are calculated by dividing the net loss attributable to ordinary
shareholders by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the year
(adjusted for the effects of potentially dilutive options and dilutive partly paid contributing shares).
The following reflects the loss and share data used to calculate basic and diluted earnings per share:

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Note 25 income tax — "No income tax is payable by the Group" and unrecognised deferred tax assets** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 60]. The tax reconciliation shows a $3,195k theoretical benefit fully offset by $3,084k "tax effect of tax losses not recognised" plus $111k prior-year over-provision, netting to nil. This confirms the Group carries a large unrecognised DTA: Australian gross tax losses ~$32.19m, SA tax losses ~ZAR32.57m (~$2.85m), and SA unredeemed capex ZAR1,475m (~$128.7m). **Forecast implication**: no cash tax in the forecast horizon until taxable profits emerge; the ZAR1,475m unredeemed capex is a substantial future shield against Prieska mining income. Verify in Note 5 / D010 whether any deferred tax liability exists (the note says "except to the extent that it does not offset a net deferred tax liability" — implying a DTL exists somewhere, likely on the Triple Flag contract liability or fair-value adjustments).

- **Note 25 — "Non-assessable income" $(1,070)k** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 60]. This is a tax-reconciliation deduction, not a P&L line. It likely includes the day-one gain on IDC extinguishment (Q122) and/or BHP Xplor grant (Q139). **Forecast implication**: confirms these items are non-taxable; does not locate them in P&L.

- **Note 26 — "Shares are anti-dilutive"** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 61]. The diluted loss per share equals basic because options/partly-paid contributing shares are anti-dilutive in a loss year. **Forecast implication**: no dilution adjustment to EPS while loss-making; but the 7,975,198,903 weighted average shares (vs 6,820,023,048 FY25) confirms ~1.155bn share increase during FY26 — consistent with the ~$34m equity raise (Q97). Confirm exact closing share count in Note 12 / D010.

- **Note 26.2 — NCI loss attribution $3,171k** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 61]. Loss attributable to NCI $3,171k vs FY25 $3,117k. **Forecast implication**: NCI absorbs ~25% of group loss ($3,171k / $12,687k), consistent with the post-IDC-conversion NCI step-up (Q113). Confirm NCI share of future Prieska profits once in production — this materially affects attributable cash flow.

- **Note 27 — Segment reporting: Australia vs South Africa** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 61]. Key observations:
  - SA segment net operating loss $(7,696)k vs Australia $(4,991)k. Australia loss is large relative to its asset base ($24,713k) — likely corporate/head-office costs and ASX listing costs.
  - SA segment total assets $148,673k vs total liabilities $51,840k → SA net assets $96,833k. Australia net assets $23,623k.
  - **Anomaly**: SA segment finance income $4,766k but finance expense $(5,330)k — net SA finance cost only $(564)k despite ~$126m PCZM (Pty) Ltd non-current liabilities. This reinforces that most SA debt is intercompany (eliminated) or non-interest-bearing/IFRS 9-discounted (Q110/Q126).
  - **Anomaly**: "Exploration expenditure written off and expensed" Australia $199k (positive, i.e., a credit/reversal?) vs SA $(2,849)k. The Australia positive $199k is unusual — possibly a reversal of prior write-off or a reclassification. Verify in Note 5.
  - **FY25 comparative**: SA finance expense $(6,600)k vs FY26 $(5,330)k — a $1,270k decline despite new IDC/Landmark loans. Consistent with IFRS 9 discounting reducing carrying-value interest, or repayment/conversion of higher-rate debt. Verify in Note 19 continuation.

- **Note 28 — Parent entity: "total net assets of the Parent Entity exceed those of the consolidated Group"** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 62]. Parent net assets $159,821k vs consolidated (implied ~$120,456k from segment: $173,386k assets − $52,930k liabilities). The ~$39m difference is the carrying value of investments in subsidiaries/loans that are impaired or loss-making at subsidiary level. **Forecast implication**: the parent's loans to subsidiaries ($147,156k non-current assets) are the funding conduit; directors assert no impairment because "loans... are recoverable once the projects are in production." This is a key going-concern/impairment assumption — if Prieska funding is delayed, parent-level impairment risk rises. Verify in D010 / Note 5.

- **Note 28 — "The Company has issued bank guarantees in respect of its mining tenements"** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 62]. Confirms the Note 24 guarantees ($5.12m SA + $0.22m Victorian) are parent-issued financial guarantee contracts. **Forecast implication**: these are contingent liabilities, not restricted cash; the $5,345k rehabilitation bonds in Note 8 are a separate balance-sheet item. Reconcile in D010.

- **Note 28 — "provisions are not required... as it is not probable that a future sacrifice... or the amount is not capable of reliable measurement"** [D012.9, physical PDF p. 62]. Standard boilerplate; no quantification. Note the tension with Note 24's quantified contingent liabilities (Agterskot ZAR97.05m, etc.) — the parent has not provided for these because they are contingent, not probable.

10% / strengthen by 10% against the ZAR (2025: 10% weaken / 10% strengthen), with all other variables
held constant, the Groups loss before tax for the year would have been $1.27 million lower / $1.27 million
higher (2025: $1.53 million lower / $1.53 million higher). The change is the expected overall volatility of
the ZAR:AUD, based on management’s assessment of the possible fluctuations, with consideration given
to the last 6 months of the reporting period and spot rate at reporting date.

 29.2 Credit risk                                                  
 Credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Group if a customer or counterparty to a financial instrument
 fails to meet its contractual obligations and arises principally from the Group’s receivables from
 customers and investment securities.                              
                                                                   
 The Group does not presently have customers and consequently does not have credit exposure to
 outstanding receivables. Other receivables represent security bonds and deposits. Trade and other
 receivables are neither past due nor impaired.                    
                                                                   
 29.3 Liquidity risk                                               
 Liquidity risk is the risk that the Group will not be able to meet its financial obligations as they fall due.
 The Group’s approach to managing liquidity is to ensure, as far as possible, that it will always have
 sufficient liquidity to meet its liabilities when due, under both normal and stressed conditions, without
 incurring unacceptable losses or risking damage to the Group’s reputation. Refer to Note 2.1.3 for a
 summary of the Group’s current plans for managing its liquidity risk.
 The Group’s objective is to maintain a balance between continuity of funding and flexibility. The Group’s
 exposure to financial obligations relating to corporate administration and projects expenditure, are
 subject to budgeting and reporting controls, to ensure that such obligations do not exceed cash held and
 known cash inflows for a period of at least one year.             
                                                                   
 Fair value of financial assets and liabilities                    
 The fair value of cash and cash equivalents and non-interest bearing financial assets and financial
 liabilities of the Group is equal to their carrying value. The carrying amounts of trade and other
 receivables and trade and other payables are assumed to approximate their fair values due to their short-
 term nature. The fair value of financial liabilities is estimated by discounting the remaining contractual
 maturities at the current market interest rate that is available for similar financial liabilities.
 29.3.1 Commodity price risk                                       
 The Group’s exposure to price risk is minimal at this stage of the operations. Commodity price risk is the
 risk that the value of a financial instrument or cash flows associated with the instrument will fluctuate
 due to changes in market rates. The risk arises from fluctuations in financial assets and liabilities that
 the Group uses.

29.3.2 Capital management
The Group’s objectives when managing capital are to safeguard the Group’s ability to continue as a
going concern in order to provide returns for shareholders and benefits for other stakeholders. The
management of the Group’s capital is performed by the Board.
The Board manages the Group’s liquidity ratio to ensure that it meets its financial obligations as they fall
due and specifically allowing for the expenditure commitments for its mining tenements to ensure that
the Group’s main assets are not at risk.
Refer to Note 2.1.3 for a summary of the Group’s current plan for managing its going concern.
None of the Group’s entities are subject to externally imposed capital requirements.

### [SECTION READING RESPONSE / DETERMINATION]
### 1. Answers to Stored Questions for This Section

**Q1 [High]: FX rates used (actual & guidance), hedging disclosures, USD/ZAR cost split or sensitivity.**
- **Status**: `Partially resolved (remainder stays open for D012.10 continuation / D013)`
- **Answer & evidence**: Note 29.1.1 discloses a ZAR:AUD sensitivity only — a 10% AUD weaken/strengthen against ZAR moves loss before tax by $1.27m lower/higher (2025: $1.53m) [D012.10, physical PDF p. 63]. Critically, the note states the Group "has not formalised a foreign currency risk management policy" — i.e. **no hedging programme disclosed** [p. 62]. The FX exposure table [p. 63] is denominated in ZAR/GBP/EUR, not USD, and the sensitivity is framed ZAR:AUD, not ZAR:USD. No USD/ZAR rate, closing rate, or average rate is stated in this section. ### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Footnote markers `[^co][^nt][^in][^ue][^d]` on the Note 29 heading [D012.10, pp. 63, 64, 65]**: These markers appear on the section heading but **no footnote definitions are present in this capture**. This is the same unresolved legend issue flagged in Q117 for Note 17.2. The markers likely denote something like "consolidated / notes / in thousands / unaudited / dollars" but this must not be assumed. **Verification question raised** (see Q153 below).

- **"The Group has not formalised a foreign currency risk management policy" [D012.10, p. 62]**: This is a material qualification. It means the Group runs **unhedged ZAR/AUD exposure**. For forecasting, this implies: (a) no hedge book to model; (b) FX gains/losses flow fully to P&L (consistent with the $421k net FX gain in Note 21, Q141); (c) the ±$1.27m PBT sensitivity is a direct, unhedged earnings swing. It also means the ZAR/USD rate used for translation is a pure spot/average rate with no hedging offset — reinforcing the need to pin the rate (Q98/Q120).

- **"During the year, the Group had one variable rate interest bearing liability" [D012.10, p. 62]**: This is a striking statement. It implies that of all the Group's debt (IDC shareholder loan, IDC/Landmark NOM loans, instalment sale, leases), only **one** is variable-rate. Yet Note 29.3.2 classifies the $30,897k "Loans" as **0.00% non-interest-bearing** [p. 64]. This creates a three-way tension: (i) Note 19.2 says the IDC shareholder loan is at SA prime (variable); (ii) Note 29.1 says one variable-rate liability exists; (iii) Note 29.3.2 says loans are non-interest-bearing. **This must be reconciled** — it directly affects the finance-expense forecast (Q103/Q119/Q146).

- **Interest rate sensitivity: "1% variation... interest revenue changing by up to $144,601... based on year-end cash balances, and up to $54,351... based on year-end security bonds and deposits" [D012.10, p. 62]**: The $144,601 on ~$14,460k cash implies ~1.0% — consistent. The $54,351 on ~$5,435k bonds implies ~1.0% — consistent. This confirms the bonds are interest-bearing (7.82% per p. 64) and cash is floating (4.66%). For forecasting, interest income on cash is modest (~$0.67m at 4.66% on $14.46m) and should be modelled as floating.

- **"The Group does not presently have customers and consequently does not have credit exposure to outstanding receivables" [D012.10, p. 63]**: Confirms **pre-revenue status** at 30 Jun 2026 — no sales, no trade receivables from customers. Critical for forecasting: FY26 has zero revenue; FY27 revenue depends entirely on Prieska first concentrate (Q10/Q29).

- **"The Group's exposure to price risk is minimal at this stage of the operations" [D012.10, p. 63]**: Confirms **no commodity hedging and no commodity price exposure yet** — consistent with pre-production. Once Prieska produces, this changes; the forecast must introduce Cu/Zn price exposure from first concentrate.

- **"The fair value of financial liabilities is estimated by discounting the remaining contractual maturities at the current market interest rate" [D012.10, p. 63]**: All financial assets/liabilities are carried at **amortised cost** (fair value column is nil throughout) [p. 64]. This confirms no fair-value-through-P&L instruments — simplifies forecasting (no mark-to-market volatility except FX).

- **"None of the Group's entities are subject to externally imposed capital requirements" [D012.10, p. 64]**: Relevant to covenant analysis — no regulatory capital covenants, but this does **not** mean no lender covenants (Glencore/IDC covenants still to check, Q9/Q24).

- **Maturity table total $4,163k (leases) vs balance-sheet $1,790k [D012.10, p. 64]**: The maturity table shows **undiscounted contractual cash flows** ($4,163k) vs carrying value ($1,790k) — a $2,373k difference representing future interest. Similarly instalment sale $782k (maturity) vs $781k (carrying) — minimal discount. This is a presentation nuance, not an error, but confirms the lease is long-dated (2–5yr bucket $3,225k).

- **"Other receivables" $5,727k (Note 7) in fair-value table [p. 64] vs $5,435k in maturity table [p. 64]**: A $292k difference between the two tables on the same page. The fair-value table shows $5,727k; the maturity table shows $5,435k. This is an internal inconsistency within Note 29 that should be flagged (Q154 below).

The 2025 detailed total (107,000,000) also does not match the 2025 closing balance (117,000,000) — a 10,000,000 gap in the prior year too. This suggests the detailed table may exclude certain grants (e.g., director/CEO options reported in the Remuneration Report, per the Note 31 text: "Options granted to Directors and CEO during the year, are reported in the Remuneration Report"). If so, ~48.5m options are held by directors/CEO and not in the detailed table. This matters for dilution forecasting and for reconciling to Note 26 weighted average shares (Q147). Verification question Q163.

- **Note 31 share-based payment expense $1.01m vs Note 21.1 $1,895k** [D012.11 p.65 vs D012.8 p.59]: A $885k discrepancy. Possible explanations: Note 21.1 may include on-charge/other equity-settled items, or Note 31 may be a subset (employee benefit expense only). This directly affects FY26 operating cost base and FY27 run-rate. Verification question Q164.

- **Note 31 "Options which expired during the financial year... were written back to accumulated losses, $0.27 million"** [D012.11, p. 65]: This is a reserve reclassification (equity-to-equity), not a P&L item — but it confirms the 27m expired options were unvested/forfeited, so no further expense will be recognised on them. Relevant to FY27 share-based payment run-rate.

- **Note 30 auditor remuneration** [D012.11, p. 65]: Total $294,060 (2025: $250,366), split Forvis Mazars Australia $123,682, Forvis Mazars South Africa $131,634, Fin5 South Africa $38,744. No non-audit fees disclosed — implies no material non-audit services. Minor forecast input; no hidden caveat.

- **Note 32.2 related-party payments** [D012.11, p. 66]: Tarney Holdings (Chairman) payments rose to $303,750 from $60,000 — a 5x increase. "Potential payments due" $10,000 (2025: $92,500). Kinsella (former CEO) nil (2025: $126,001). The Tarney step-up is a recurring governance cost to carry into FY27 administration expenses. No footnote caveat beyond the entity descriptions.

- **Note 33 subsequent events** [D012.11, p. 66]: Standard clean statement — no material subsequent events. This is a negative confirmation; it does not resolve the funding-close timing question (Q29) but confirms no post-balance-date event changed the picture before the report date.

### 2. Footnote & Qualification Deep-Dive

- **Material uncertainty related to going concern [D013, physical PDF p. 68]**: The auditor explicitly draws attention to Note 2.1.3, citing the **net loss of AU$12.69m** and stating a **material uncertainty exists that may cast significant doubt on the Group's ability to continue as a going concern**. The opinion is **not modified**. Implication for forecasting: this is the single most important qualification in the report. It confirms the Group is not yet self-funding and that the forecast must be built on an explicit funding-close assumption (ties Q3, Q10, Q29, Q50). The AU$12.69m net loss is a hard anchor for the FY26 base case and should reconcile to the D010-ins / D012.9 loss figure (Q149 cites $12,687k group loss — consistent to rounding).
- **Key audit matter — Existence and valuation of exploration assets [D013, p. 69]**: The auditor identifies capitalised E&E as a **significant asset** and states procedures included confirming **tenure/rights current at reporting date and likelihood of renewal for expiring rights**, agreeing capitalised spend to supporting documentation, and reviewing **directors' impairment-indicator assessment**. Implication: the auditor did **not** flag an impairment, which supports carrying the $90,939k deferred E&E and $6,809k exploration rights at book (ties Q93). But the emphasis on "likelihood of renewal for expiring rights" signals tenure-renewal risk that must be checked against the tenement/commitment disclosures (Q136, Q143).
- **Key audit matter scope note [D013, p. 69]**: Only **one** key audit matter is listed (exploration assets). Notably, **no KAM is raised on**: the IDC convertible conversion / day-one gain (Q122), the Triple Flag GRR contract liability (Q123), the preference-share receivable exceeding principal (Q89), or the going-concern-sensitive NOM/Okiep funding (Q114/Q134). This is a useful negative signal — the auditor did not consider these material enough to be KAMs — but it does **not** resolve the underlying reconciliation questions, which remain open.
- **"Other information" section [D013, p. 69]**: Auditor states "We have nothing to report in this regard" on other information (which includes the Remuneration Report, subject to separate assurance). No inconsistency flagged between narrative sections and the financial report.
- **Remuneration Report opinion [D013, p. 70]**: Unqualified section 300A opinion; Remuneration Report located at **pages 77–85** — outside the current Report Map and not captured. This is the target for Q165 and Q28 (individual KMP remuneration).
- **No footnote markers (`[^1]`, `*`) appear in the D013 capture** — the auditor's report contains no table footnotes requiring definition. Q153 (marker legend) is therefore **not** resolvable from D013 and must be sought in Note 1/2 or a front-of-notes legend.
